tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. ﻿function Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the devices that signed in recently and are marked compliant, for the devices-compliant measure.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The reader of the devices-compliant measure (powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1), which decides the step
    intune.devices-compliant of the defender's path. A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device
    blocks every device that Microsoft Entra ID doesn't mark compliant, so the share of compliant devices among the
    devices in use says whether such a policy can be turned on.

    Reads the enabled devices in Microsoft Entra ID that signed in within the last SignedInWithinDays days
    (approximateLastSignInDateTime), through the Graph cache. A device counts when isCompliant is true: Intune or
    an approved MDM sets it, and it is what a compliant-device grant checks. Devices that are not compliant are
    returned as the objects that fall short, most recent sign-in first, whether they are managed (isManaged) and
    noncompliant or not managed at all.

    A device that has no Microsoft Entra identity (neither registered nor joined) can't be seen this way, so it is
    neither counted nor listed. A compliant-device policy blocks it too.

    Returns an object with Count (compliant devices), Total (devices that signed in) and Objects (the devices that
    aren't compliant, as Type, Id and DisplayName).

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare

    Returns the number of compliant devices among the enabled devices that signed in within the last 30 days.

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare -SignedInWithinDays 14

    Counts only the devices that signed in within the last 14 days.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param(
        # Devices that signed in within this many days are counted. approximateLastSignInDateTime is approximate, so
        # keep it well above a week.
        [ValidateRange(1, 365)]
        [int] $SignedInWithinDays = 30
    )

    # Start of the UTC day, so the request, and so its cache entry, stays the same for the whole day.
    $since = [datetime]::UtcNow.Date.AddDays(-$SignedInWithinDays).ToString('yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ', [cultureinfo]::InvariantCulture)
    $deviceSplat = @{
        RelativeUri     = 'devices'
        Filter          = "accountEnabled eq true and approximateLastSignInDateTime ge $since"
        # isManaged, operatingSystem and trustType are read for the object facts device.managed, device.os and
        # device.joinType (design section 12), which this reader writes once Add-MtAffectedObjectFact takes a Key.
        Select          = 'id', 'displayName', 'approximateLastSignInDateTime', 'isCompliant', 'isManaged', 'operatingSystem', 'trustType'
        QueryParameters = @{ '$count' = 'true' }
    }
    $devices = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest @deviceSplat | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })

    $notCompliant = @($devices | Where-Object { $_.isCompliant -ne $true })

    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
        Count   = $devices.Count - $notCompliant.Count
        Total   = $devices.Count
        Objects = @(
            $notCompliant |
                Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { $_.approximateLastSignInDateTime -as [datetime] }; Descending = $true }, displayName, id |
                ForEach-Object {
                    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
                        Type        = 'Device'
                        Id          = [string]$_.id
                        DisplayName = [string]$_.displayName
                    }
                }
        )
    }
}
﻿function Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Counts the enabled member users who are registered for multifactor authentication, for the mfa-registered
    measure.

    .DESCRIPTION
    The reader of the mfa-registered measure (powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1), which decides the step
    entra.mfa-registered of the defender's path. User-risk and sign-in-risk policies ask users to complete MFA, and
    a user who hasn't registered a method can't, so the share of registered users says whether those policies can
    be turned on.

    Reads the authentication methods registration report (reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails),
    which needs Microsoft Entra ID P1, through the Graph cache. A member user counts when isMfaRegistered is true.
    Left out of the count:

    - disabled users, which the report also lists;
    - the emergency access accounts in the Maester configuration (EmergencyAccessAccounts), and the users in the
      emergency access groups it names, because they stay excluded from these policies;
    - the users that hold a directory synchronization role, which Conditional Access policies exclude too.

    A configured emergency access account that can't be found stops the reader with an error, as it does in the
    checks that read them, so the figure never counts an account that should have been left out.

    Returns an object with Count (registered users), Total (the users counted) and Objects (the users who aren't
    registered, as Type, Id and DisplayName, administrators first).

    .EXAMPLE
    Get-MtMfaRegistrationShare

    Returns the number of enabled member users who are registered for MFA, apart from the emergency access and
    directory synchronization accounts.
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([pscustomobject])]
    param()

    # The whole report, with no $select or $filter, so other readers of the report share its cache entry.
    $registrations = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails' | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })

    $excluded = [System.Collections.Generic.HashSet[string]]::new([System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)
    foreach ($user in @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'users' -Filter 'accountEnabled eq false' -Select 'id' | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ })) {
        $null = $excluded.Add([string]$user.id)
    }
    foreach ($account in @(Get-MtEmergencyAccessAccount)) {
        if ($account.Type -eq 'group') {
            $groupUsers = @(Get-MtGroupMember -GroupId $account.ObjectId -Recursive | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -eq '#microsoft.graph.user' })
            foreach ($member in $groupUsers) { $null = $excluded.Add([string]$member.id) }
        } elseif ($account.ObjectId) {
            $null = $excluded.Add([string]$account.ObjectId)
        }
    }
    foreach ($member in @(Get-MtRoleMember -Role 'DirectorySynchronizationAccounts', 'OnPremisesDirectorySyncAccount' | Where-Object { $_.'@odata.type' -ne '#microsoft.graph.servicePrincipal' })) {
        if ($member.id) { $null = $excluded.Add([string]$member.id) }
    }

    $users = @($registrations | Where-Object { $_.userType -eq 'member' -and $_.id -and -not $excluded.Contains([string]$_.id) })
    $notRegistered = @($users | Where-Object { $_.isMfaRegistered -ne $true })

    # The object facts user.mfaRegistered (design section 12), under the object ID and the UPN, are written for
    # these users once Add-MtAffectedObjectFact takes a Key.
    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
        Count   = $users.Count - $notRegistered.Count
        Total   = $users.Count
        Objects = @(
            $notRegistered |
                Sort-Object -Property @{ Expression = { $_.isAdmin -eq $true }; Descending = $true }, userPrincipalName, id |
                ForEach-Object {
                    [pscustomobject][ordered]@{
                        Type        = 'User'
                        Id          = [string]$_.id
                        DisplayName = if ($_.userDisplayName) { [string]$_.userDisplayName } else { [string]$_.userPrincipalName }
                    }
                }
        )
    }
}

425	  `Invoke-Maester -TestId MT.1001 -IncludePrerequisites`. The How to fix tab adds the step's rollout.
426	- **Overview.** One card: Ready now, Blocked and Check first counts, with a link to the action plan.
427	- **Small runs.** With one to three tests that ran, there are no lanes. Each test page carries "Before you fix
428	  this" (section 10).
429	
430	The report reads `Steps` and `Goals` as written and works out nothing itself.
431	
432	## 10. Scoping rules
433	
434	The rule for every output: scope everything to what ran, and never infer a status for a test that did not run.
435	
436	| Run | Report | Console | Result |
437	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
438	| Full run | Groups and a lane for every goal in scope | The summary line | `Steps`, `Goals` |
439	| One suite or product | Only goals with a step in scope. A step whose tests were not selected shows "Not checked in this run" and the command to include them | The line, when a step is in scope | The steps in scope, with all their tests |
440	| One to three tests | No lanes. "Before you fix this" on each test page, with the measures of the prerequisites and `Earlier` statuses with their dates | Nothing extra | The same |
441	| Tests that name no step (GitHub, Azure DevOps, Active Directory, most custom tests) | No change. The views stay hidden | No change | No `Steps` |
442	| A verifying test that couldn't run, or a measure that couldn't be read (service not connected, no licence, missing permission) | The step is Unknown, with the reason and the fix command, and never Not done | Counted with the tests that didn't run | `Status` `Unknown` with the reason codes |
443	
444	## 11. Measures
445	
446	<<<<<<< HEAD
447	Seven steps in the first catalogue have no check. Two of them are tenant states that a figure from Graph
448	settles, so in Phase 1 they get measures, not tests. The owner ruled on 5 November 2026 that readiness is a data
449	point, not a test. A share of compliant devices isn't a misconfiguration and has no meaningful severity or
450	ATT&CK technique, so it must not change pass rates or the test count. A measure also runs whenever its step is
451	in scope, so "Before you fix this" shows a real figure even after a one-test run, where a test would have had
452	to be selected.
453	=======
454	17 of the 43 steps in the first catalogue have no Maester check (section 15). Two of them get readiness checks in Phase 1. Each check is a native
455	test in `tests/maester/<service>/`. It reads Graph through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers,
456	reports a count and a share, and lists the objects that hold the step back as affected objects. It passes when
457	the share is at least its `MinimumShare` parameter (an `int`, default `95`).
458	>>>>>>> claude/defenders-path-m2-8b8ecc
459	
460	A measure is an entry in the measure registry, `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`:
461	
462	```powershell
463	@{
464	    Measures = @(
465	        @{
466	            Key         = 'devices-compliant'
467	            Function    = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
468	            Title       = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
469	            Unit        = 'devices'
470	            Service     = 'Graph'
471	            License     = 'INTUNE_A'
472	            Permission  = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All'
473	        }
474	    )
475	}
476	```
477	
478	- `Service`, `License` and `Permission` use the grammar of the test attributes, and the engine applies them the
479	  way it gates a test. A measure whose gate fails is Unknown with the matching reason code.
480	- `Function` names an internal reader in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`. It reads through the Graph
481	  cache and returns `Count` (the objects that meet the bar), `Total`, and `Objects` (those that fall short, as
482	  `Type`, `Id` and `DisplayName`). The engine keeps up to 100 of them.
483	- The engine works out `Share`, compares it with the step's `MinimumShare` or the run config's override, and
484	  writes the result to the step (section 7.2).
485	- Readers write object facts with the shared keys (section 12) for the objects they list.
486	
487	| Key | Step | Reads | Notes |
488	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
489	| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Entra `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | The objects are the devices a compliant-device policy would block. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so |
490	| `mfa-registered` | `entra.mfa-registered` | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` for enabled member users | Needs Entra ID P1. Leaves out the emergency access accounts |
491	
492	Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
493	password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
494	Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
495	see the devices that have no identity yet. The emergency access accounts holding Global Administrator as a
496	permanent active assignment is another state with no Maester check.
497	
498	The Defender–Intune connector is not covered. MT.1098 checks the health of the Mobile Threat Defense connectors it
499	finds, and skips or passes when the Defender connector is missing. The `defender-device-risk` goal needs four
500	checks before Maester can follow it: the Defender connector is enabled, its compliance toggle is on for each
501	platform that has a compliance policy, and Windows and Android Enterprise compliance policies require a machine
502	risk score.
503	
504	A measure isn't a test: it has no ID, no row in `Tests` and no attribute review, and it plays no part in pass
505	rates, frameworks or the test count. Packs can't add measures in Phase 1.
506	
507	## 12. Object facts
508	
509	The Zero Trust facts work (`Add-MtAffectedObjectFact`, maester365/maester#2681) puts facts on
510	listed objects: join type, managed and compliant for devices, MFA and passwordless for users. They are the
511	drill-down behind a lane ("38 devices aren't managed"). They can't replace measures, because facts attach
512	only to objects the run lists and come from the Zero Trust export only when it ran. Measures write facts too.
513	
514	This design asked that work to give each fact a stable key and a raw value before the command ships, so that a
515	lane's drill-down never parses display text. It did, in maester365/maester#2681: a fact has `Name`, `Value`
516	(display text), `Tone`, an optional `Key` (dotted camelCase, `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)+$`), an
517	optional `Raw` (boolean, number, string, string list, or ISO 8601 UTC date), `Source` and `AsOf`. A fact with the
518	same `Key` from the same `Source` replaces the earlier one. The shared keys are listed under "Fact keys" in
519	`website/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results.md`. The ones this design reads:
520	
521	| Key | Raw | Used for |
522	| --- | --- | --- |
523	| `device.managed`, `device.compliant` | bool | The devices behind `intune.devices-compliant`. Management and compliance are separate facts |
524	| `device.joinType` | `AzureAd`, `ServerAd` or `Workplace` | Join coverage, for hybrid join and token protection |
525	| `device.os` | string | Which platforms need a compliance policy |
526	| `user.mfaRegistered`, `user.passwordless` | bool | The users behind `entra.mfa-registered` and the phishing-resistant steps |
527	| `user.privilegedRoles` | string list | The admins step of phishing-resistant MFA, and the privileged access goal |
528	| `signIn.daysSince` | int, or null when none is recorded | Leaving out stale devices and users. Counted from the fact's `AsOf`, not from now |
529	
530	User facts are recorded under both the object ID and the UPN, so a record has them whichever way it was keyed.
531	The measures write the same keys for the objects they list.
532	
533	## 13. Keeping the catalogue current
534	
535	The sources are the nine Learn mirrors built with `merill/learn-mirror`. They crawl Learn four times a day and
536	make one commit per changed page. They cover Entra, Intune, Defender, security (Zero Trust), Purview, Teams,
537	SharePoint, Exchange and Windows Server. The tooling lives in `build/steps/`:
538	
539	| Script | Job |
540	| --- | --- |
541	| `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` | Clones or updates the mirrors into a cache folder, and builds a URL-to-file index. Old URLs are followed through Learn's redirects: 23 of the 77 Intune and Defender links in check guides are redirects today |
542	| `Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1` | For the Learn pages that check guides and catalogue sources link, pulls the prerequisite sections and sentences ("before you", "first", "must", "won't work without") with their file and line. Writes proposals as JSON for a maintainer, and optionally asks a model to reword them as `Note` text. Nothing enters the catalogue without review |
543	| `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` | For each source, lists the mirror commits to its file since `Reviewed`. Exits non-zero when any changed |
544	
545	A scheduled workflow, `.github/workflows/step-sources.yaml`, runs `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` weekly and keeps one
546	issue open that lists the steps whose sources changed, with the diff link for each. It opens issues, never pull
547	requests. A maintainer re-reads the page and bumps `Reviewed`.
548	
549	The unit tests make no network calls. They check that every `Url` is a well-formed Learn URL. Only the workflow
550	checks it against the mirrors.
551	
552	## 14. Enforcement
553	
554	`powershell/tests/general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`:
555	
556	- every file matches the schema and has no unknown keys;
557	- step IDs are unique, their product key is in the taxonomy, and the file they are in is named after that key;
558	- every ID in `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf`, `RecommendedFirst`, `Conflicts` and a goal's `Step` exists;
559	- every `RequiresOneOf` group has at least two steps, and no step names the same step in two relationships;
560	- `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf` and `RecommendedFirst` together have no cycle, and the message names the cycle;
561	- every `OnlyWhen` key is a known condition;
562	- every step has a source, every `Note` is 200 characters or less, and maintainer-only sources are under 10%
563	  of all sources;
564	- every step belongs to at least one goal, and goal IDs are unique;
565	- every `Measure` key is in the measure registry and its `MinimumShare` is from 1 to 100, and every registry
566	  entry names a reader function the module has.
567	
568	`Get-MtStepProblem` makes these checks, plus two about the tests: every `Step` that a built-in test or a
569	`packs/*/taxonomy.json` names exists, and (with `-Coverage`, over every built-in test) `Unchecked` is set exactly
570	on the steps that no test names and that have no `Measure`. `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` fails on all of them except the `Unchecked`
571	check, because the build can run on a folder that holds only some of the tests. A run only warns about a step
572	the catalogue does not have.
573	
574	## 15. The first catalogue
575	
576	Milestone M2 checked every step and relationship against the Learn mirrors on 5 November 2026. Where Learn
577	disagreed with the draft, Learn won. The catalogue has 43 steps (27 Entra, 9 Intune, 7 Defender) in eight goals,
578	with 76 sources. All of them cite Learn; none cites a maintainer. 43 tests name a step: 37 hand-written tests,

`Invoke-Maester -TestId MT.1001 -IncludePrerequisites`. The How to fix tab adds the step's rollout.
- **Overview.** One card: Ready now, Blocked and Check first counts, with a link to the action plan.
- **Small runs.** With one to three tests that ran, there are no lanes. Each test page carries "Before you fix
  this" (section 10).

The report reads `Steps` and `Goals` as written and works out nothing itself.

## 10. Scoping rules

The rule for every output: scope everything to what ran, and never infer a status for a test that did not run.

| Run | Report | Console | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Full run | Groups and a lane for every goal in scope | The summary line | `Steps`, `Goals` |
| One suite or product | Only goals with a step in scope. A step whose tests were not selected shows "Not checked in this run" and the command to include them | The line, when a step is in scope | The steps in scope, with all their tests |
| One to three tests | No lanes. "Before you fix this" on each test page, with the measures of the prerequisites and `Earlier` statuses with their dates | Nothing extra | The same |
| Tests that name no step (GitHub, Azure DevOps, Active Directory, most custom tests) | No change. The views stay hidden | No change | No `Steps` |
| A verifying test that couldn't run, or a measure that couldn't be read (service not connected, no licence, missing permission) | The step is Unknown, with the reason and the fix command, and never Not done | Counted with the tests that didn't run | `Status` `Unknown` with the reason codes |

## 11. Measures

Seven steps in the first catalogue have no check. Two of them are tenant states that a figure from Graph
settles, so in Phase 1 they get measures, not tests. The owner ruled on 5 November 2026 that readiness is a data
point, not a test. A share of compliant devices isn't a misconfiguration and has no meaningful severity or
ATT&CK technique, so it must not change pass rates or the test count. A measure also runs whenever its step is
in scope, so "Before you fix this" shows a real figure even after a one-test run, where a test would have had
to be selected.
=======
17 of the 43 steps in the first catalogue have no Maester check (section 15). Two of them get readiness checks in Phase 1. Each check is a native
test in `tests/maester/<service>/`. It reads Graph through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers,
reports a count and a share, and lists the objects that hold the step back as affected objects. It passes when
the share is at least its `MinimumShare` parameter (an `int`, default `95`).
>>>>>>> claude/defenders-path-m2-8b8ecc

A measure is an entry in the measure registry, `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`:

```powershell
@{
    Measures = @(
        @{
            Key         = 'devices-compliant'
            Function    = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
            Title       = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
            Unit        = 'devices'
            Service     = 'Graph'
            License     = 'INTUNE_A'
            Permission  = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All'
        }
    )
}
```

- `Service`, `License` and `Permission` use the grammar of the test attributes, and the engine applies them the
  way it gates a test. A measure whose gate fails is Unknown with the matching reason code.
- `Function` names an internal reader in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`. It reads through the Graph
  cache and returns `Count` (the objects that meet the bar), `Total`, and `Objects` (those that fall short, as
  `Type`, `Id` and `DisplayName`). The engine keeps up to 100 of them.
- The engine works out `Share`, compares it with the step's `MinimumShare` or the run config's override, and
  writes the result to the step (section 7.2).
- Readers write object facts with the shared keys (section 12) for the objects they list.

| Key | Step | Reads | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Entra `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | The objects are the devices a compliant-device policy would block. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so |
| `mfa-registered` | `entra.mfa-registered` | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` for enabled member users | Needs Entra ID P1. Leaves out the emergency access accounts |

Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
see the devices that have no identity yet. The emergency access accounts holding Global Administrator as a
permanent active assignment is another state with no Maester check.

The Defender–Intune connector is not covered. MT.1098 checks the health of the Mobile Threat Defense connectors it
finds, and skips or passes when the Defender connector is missing. The `defender-device-risk` goal needs four
checks before Maester can follow it: the Defender connector is enabled, its compliance toggle is on for each
platform that has a compliance policy, and Windows and Android Enterprise compliance policies require a machine
risk score.

A measure isn't a test: it has no ID, no row in `Tests` and no attribute review, and it plays no part in pass
rates, frameworks or the test count. Packs can't add measures in Phase 1.

## 12. Object facts

The Zero Trust facts work (`Add-MtAffectedObjectFact`, maester365/maester#2681) puts facts on
listed objects: join type, managed and compliant for devices, MFA and passwordless for users. They are the
drill-down behind a lane ("38 devices aren't managed"). They can't replace measures, because facts attach
only to objects the run lists and come from the Zero Trust export only when it ran. Measures write facts too.

This design asked that work to give each fact a stable key and a raw value before the command ships, so that a
lane's drill-down never parses display text. It did, in maester365/maester#2681: a fact has `Name`, `Value`
(display text), `Tone`, an optional `Key` (dotted camelCase, `^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*(\.[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]*)+$`), an
optional `Raw` (boolean, number, string, string list, or ISO 8601 UTC date), `Source` and `AsOf`. A fact with the
same `Key` from the same `Source` replaces the earlier one. The shared keys are listed under "Fact keys" in
`website/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results.md`. The ones this design reads:

| Key | Raw | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device.managed`, `device.compliant` | bool | The devices behind `intune.devices-compliant`. Management and compliance are separate facts |
| `device.joinType` | `AzureAd`, `ServerAd` or `Workplace` | Join coverage, for hybrid join and token protection |
| `device.os` | string | Which platforms need a compliance policy |
| `user.mfaRegistered`, `user.passwordless` | bool | The users behind `entra.mfa-registered` and the phishing-resistant steps |
| `user.privilegedRoles` | string list | The admins step of phishing-resistant MFA, and the privileged access goal |
| `signIn.daysSince` | int, or null when none is recorded | Leaving out stale devices and users. Counted from the fact's `AsOf`, not from now |

User facts are recorded under both the object ID and the UPN, so a record has them whichever way it was keyed.
The measures write the same keys for the objects they list.

## 13. Keeping the catalogue current

The sources are the nine Learn mirrors built with `merill/learn-mirror`. They crawl Learn four times a day and
make one commit per changed page. They cover Entra, Intune, Defender, security (Zero Trust), Purview, Teams,
SharePoint, Exchange and Windows Server. The tooling lives in `build/steps/`:

| Script | Job |
| --- | --- |
| `Update-MtLearnMirror.ps1` | Clones or updates the mirrors into a cache folder, and builds a URL-to-file index. Old URLs are followed through Learn's redirects: 23 of the 77 Intune and Defender links in check guides are redirects today |
| `Find-MtStepCandidate.ps1` | For the Learn pages that check guides and catalogue sources link, pulls the prerequisite sections and sentences ("before you", "first", "must", "won't work without") with their file and line. Writes proposals as JSON for a maintainer, and optionally asks a model to reword them as `Note` text. Nothing enters the catalogue without review |
| `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` | For each source, lists the mirror commits to its file since `Reviewed`. Exits non-zero when any changed |

A scheduled workflow, `.github/workflows/step-sources.yaml`, runs `Test-MtStepSource.ps1` weekly and keeps one
issue open that lists the steps whose sources changed, with the diff link for each. It opens issues, never pull
requests. A maintainer re-reads the page and bumps `Reviewed`.

The unit tests make no network calls. They check that every `Url` is a well-formed Learn URL. Only the workflow
checks it against the mirrors.

## 14. Enforcement

`powershell/tests/general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`:

- every file matches the schema and has no unknown keys;
- step IDs are unique, their product key is in the taxonomy, and the file they are in is named after that key;
- every ID in `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf`, `RecommendedFirst`, `Conflicts` and a goal's `Step` exists;
- every `RequiresOneOf` group has at least two steps, and no step names the same step in two relationships;
- `Requires`, `RequiresOneOf` and `RecommendedFirst` together have no cycle, and the message names the cycle;
- every `OnlyWhen` key is a known condition;
- every step has a source, every `Note` is 200 characters or less, and maintainer-only sources are under 10%
  of all sources;
- every step belongs to at least one goal, and goal IDs are unique;
- every `Measure` key is in the measure registry and its `MinimumShare` is from 1 to 100, and every registry
  entry names a reader function the module has.

`Get-MtStepProblem` makes these checks, plus two about the tests: every `Step` that a built-in test or a
`packs/*/taxonomy.json` names exists, and (with `-Coverage`, over every built-in test) `Unchecked` is set exactly
on the steps that no test names and that have no `Measure`. `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` fails on all of them except the `Unchecked`
check, because the build can run on a folder that holds only some of the tests. A run only warns about a step
the catalogue does not have.

raises user risk (howto-identity-protection-remediate-unblock).
  - Learn's rule that the two risk conditions go in separate policies is a warning, not an order. It is now in both
    steps' rollout, so `entra.ca-risk-policies-separate` and MT.1049 left the catalogue.
  - `entra.trusted-named-locations` (CIS 5.2.2.14) is new and recommended before sign-in risk. Some detections use
    trusted locations to cut false positives.
  - `entra.ca-user-risk` is `Unchecked`. Learn now recommends the Require risk remediation grant (policy-risk-based-user),
    and MT.1013 and CIS 5.2.2.6 accept only Require password change.
- **Phishing-resistant MFA.**
  - Windows Hello for Business is one of the methods that meet the phishing-resistant strength, not a link in the
    chain (concept-authentication-strengths). It is now `intune.windows-hello`, in a "one of" group with passkeys,
    certificate-based authentication and macOS Platform SSO. A tenant that uses only one of them is not blocked.
  - Registration is split into admins and all users, and enforcement requires each. Learn warns that an
    unregistered admin can lock the tenant out (policy-admin-phish-resistant-mfa).
  - The Temporary Access Pass is one of two ways to bootstrap registration, so it is recommended first, not
    required.
  - Admins come first "typically", so the admin policy is recommended before the all-users one, not required.
- **Privileged access.**
  - The draft's `entra.pim-alerts` became `entra.pim-notifications`. CISA 7.7 checks notification recipients, not
    PIM security alerts.
  - `entra.pim-approval-global-admin` (CIS 5.3.4, CISA 7.6) is new. It requires the emergency access accounts,
    because approval with no available approver locks the tenant (pim-how-to-change-default-settings).
  - Learn sets role settings before it hands out eligible assignments (pim-getting-started), so both settings steps
    are recommended first.
  - `entra.pim-roles-used` (MT.1030) left the goal. Learn treats unused roles as an alert to act on and access
    reviews as the prevention, not as a rollout step.
- **Token protection.** The step is `entra.ca-token-protection-windows`, because every test checks a Windows
  policy and Learn deploys Apple separately with its own prerequisites. Device registration is recommended first,
  not required: current Windows builds prompt unregistered users to register (deployment-guide-token-protection-windows).
  The same guide pairs the policy with blocking unknown platforms, which MT.1015 checks.
- **Email authentication.**
  - The steps are `defender.*`. Learn documents them under Defender for Office 365, DKIM is set up in the Defender
    portal, and most of the tests declare `defender`.
  - SPF and DKIM are required only by the steps that enforce DMARC. A p=none record changes no delivery, and Learn
    advises publishing one early to find senders (email-authentication-spf-configure).
  - `dmarc-monitor` became `defender.dmarc-published` (CISA 4.1).
  - CIS 2.1.10 rejects p=none, so it verifies `defender.dmarc-enforce`, which means quarantine or reject with
    reports on every domain, as the deployment guide asks (mdo-deployment-guide).
  - The goal ends at p=reject (`defender.dmarc-reject`, CISA 4.2 and MT.1182).
  - ORCA.235 fails `~all`, so it verifies its own step, `defender.spf-hard-fail`.
- **Defender device risk.**
  - Learn connects the services before it onboards devices, so the draft order is reversed.
  - The connector's per-platform compliance toggle is a step of its own (configure-integration).
  - Compliance policies are recommended first, not required, because the risk score is one setting inside them.
  - MT.1098 doesn't verify the connector (section 11). MT.1235 reads the third-party threat level on Android
    device administrator, not Defender's risk score. MT.1216 reads a macOS setting that Learn doesn't document.

function Add-MtAffectedObjectFact {
    <#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Adds facts about an object, such as its last sign-in or its expired secrets, to the Affected objects page.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Call this from a test, an instance source or a pack that knows more about an object than the checks that name
    it: when the object was last used, which permissions it holds, whether its credentials have expired. The facts
    are shown with the object on the Affected objects page of the HTML report and kept in the AffectedObjects of the
    results, the JSON output and the objects files.

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -GraphObjects says which objects a result is about, and adds them to the page with the check
    that named them. Add-MtAffectedObjectFact says what is known about an object, whichever check named it.

    Facts only describe an object that the run already lists. They are merged into the record with the same System,
    Type and Id when the results are built, so adding facts about an object that no check names adds nothing to the
    report. Facts are collected only while Invoke-Maester collects affected objects; otherwise the call does nothing.

    Each fact has a Name, a Value and a Tone: Risk for something to fix, Warning for something to review, Good for a
    sign that the object is in order, and Info (the default) for anything else.

    A fact can also carry a Key and a Raw value, for code that reads the results: a summary, an insight or another
    report. The Key names what the fact is about, from the shared list of fact keys (user.mfaRegistered,
    signIn.daysSince, device.managed...), so the same fact from two sources means the same thing. Raw is its value as
    data: a boolean, a number, a string, a list of strings or a date, which is kept as an ISO 8601 UTC string. Value
    stays the text people read. Raw is kept only with a Key. A fact without a Key is shown the same way.

    Adding a fact with the same Key, or without a Key the same Name, from the same Source again replaces the earlier one.

    The value is shown as text. Name counts rather than other people where you can: the page shows facts to everyone
    who reads the report, and -RedactUserIdentity replaces only the names of users the run knows.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Type ServicePrincipal -Id $sp.id -Source 'Contoso inventory' -Fact @(
        @{ Name = 'Last sign-in'; Value = '2026-06-15 (143 days ago)'; Tone = 'Risk' }
        @{ Name = 'Publisher'; Value = 'Third party (Contoso Ltd)' }
    )

    Adds two facts to an enterprise application.

    .EXAMPLE
    Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Type User -Id $user.id -Source 'Contoso HR' -Fact @(
        @{ Name = 'MFA'; Value = 'Not registered'; Tone = 'Risk'; Key = 'user.mfaRegistered'; Raw = $false }
        @{ Name = 'Last sign-in'; Value = '2026-06-15 (143 days ago)'; Tone = 'Warning'; Key = 'signIn.daysSince'; Raw = 143 }
    )

    Adds facts with keys, so code can read whether the user has MFA and how long since they signed in without
    parsing the text.

    .EXAMPLE
    $records | Add-MtAffectedObjectFact -Source 'Zero Trust Assessment' -AsOf $report.ExecutedAt

    Adds facts to many objects at once. Each record has Type, Id and Fact properties, and optionally System.

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Add-MtAffectedObjectFact

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results#adding-facts-about-an-object

    .LINK
    https://maester.dev/docs/writing-tests/formatting-test-results#fact-keys
    #>
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([void])]
    param(
        # The object type, as the Affected objects page records it: User, Group, ServicePrincipal, AppRegistration
        # (keyed by its appId), Device, ConditionalAccessPolicy, AgentIdentity, AgentIdentityBlueprint, ConfigurationPolicy...
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Type,

        # The object's id, the same id the record uses (for an app registration, its appId).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]
        [ValidateNotNullOrEmpty()]
        [string] $Id,

        # The facts: hashtables or objects with Name, Value, and optionally Tone (Risk, Warning, Good or Info), Key (a
        # shared fact key such as user.mfaRegistered) and Raw (its value as data).
        [Parameter(Mandatory, ValueFromPipelineByPropertyName)]

content.content:
- **Scope.** A step is in scope when a row that ran names it, or when it is a prerequisite, at any depth, of
  such a step. A goal is in scope when any of its steps is. A row ran when its result is anything but
  `NotRun`.
- **Tests come from the inventory, not only the rows.** `Tests` lists every test the engine knows that names
  the step: built-in tests from the catalog, custom tests that were discovered, and pack tests from each pack's
  catalogue. A test with no row has `Result` `NotRun` and `ReasonCode` `NotInRun`. The report can then name the
  command that checks it. This is how `Frameworks` already lists requirements that no row checks.
- **`Measure`** is set on a step that has one, whether or not it could be read:
  `{ "Key": "devices-compliant", "Count": 412, "Total": 580, "Share": 71, "MinimumShare": 95, "Met": false,
  "ReadAt": "...", "ObjectCount": 168, "Objects": [{ "Type": "Device", "Id": "...", "DisplayName": "..." }],
  "ReasonCode": null }`. `Objects` holds up to 100 of the objects that fall short. `ReasonCode` says why a measure
  couldn't be read, with the same codes a skipped test uses.
- **`Earlier`** is set on a step that is Not checked in this run when an earlier result in the output folder
  checked it: `{ "Status": "Done", "ExecutedAt": "...", "File": "..." }`. It is never mixed into this run's
  status or counts. `Get-MtPreviousResult` gains `LastKnown`, which is the newest earlier result for each test ID
  a step in scope names. It reads only files that `History` already lists, and only when some step in scope is
  Not checked. Today `Results` covers the newest earlier run only, and after a one-check run that run says

content.text: Now the three rulings: an Intune licence on the device measure, a `Caveat` field in the registry, and `isMfaCapable` for MFA.

input.description: Add the optional Caveat key to the registry reader

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old_hdr="""#   Unit        what is counted, plural, for example 'devices'
"""
new_hdr="""#   Unit        what is counted, plural, for example 'devices'
#   Caveat      one line of 200 characters or less, shown with the figure, on what it can't see or leaves out
#               (optional)
"""
assert old_hdr in s
s=s.replace(old_hdr,new_hdr)
start=s.index('@{\n    Measures = @(')
s=s[:start]+"""@{
    Measures = @(
        @{
            # Step intune.devices-compliant. isCompliant is set by Intune, also for the devices of a compliance partner,
            # which needs Intune licences as well, so a tenant without Intune has no figure to read.
            Key        = 'devices-compliant'
            Function   = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
            Title      = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
            Unit       = 'devices'
            Caveat     = "Devices that aren't registered or joined in Microsoft Entra ID can't be counted. A compliant-device policy blocks them too."
            Service    = 'Graph'
            License    = 'INTUNE_A'
            Permission = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All | Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All'
        }
        @{
            # Step entra.mfa-registered. isMfaCapable, not isMfaRegistered: the method must also be one the
            # authentication methods policy allows, or the user still can't complete MFA. The registration report needs
            # Microsoft Entra ID P1 and AuditLog.Read.All.
            Key        = 'mfa-capable'
            Function   = 'Get-MtMfaCapableShare'
            Title      = 'Enabled member users can complete MFA'
            Unit       = 'users'
            Caveat     = 'Counts only methods the authentication methods policy allows. Guests, disabled users, emergency access and directory sync accounts are left out.'
            Service    = 'Graph'
            License    = 'AAD_PREMIUM'
            Permission = ('Graph:Scope:AuditLog.Read.All', 'Graph:Scope:Directory.Read.All')
        }
    )
}
"""
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s)
EOF

| 11 | Earlier statuses | **`LastKnown` per test, read only when a step in scope is Not checked** | The newest earlier run only, which says little after a one-check run |
| 12 | Catalogue wording | **Maester's own words and a link, 200 characters at most** | Quoting Learn |
| 13 | Mining output | **Proposals for review, and a weekly issue for changed sources** | A workflow that opens pull requests |
| 14 | Fact keys | **Ask the facts work for `Key` and a raw value before it ships** | Add them later. That breaks nothing, but costs more |
| 15 | Action plan | **The defender's path leads the page, with the ranked list below** | A separate page, which keeps today's plan unchanged but hides the strong point |

- The insights step (`Insight.<ID>.ps1`), attack scenarios, the most exposed identities and the reader profile.
  They are the rest of Phase 1 and get a design of their own. Steps are the same unit as the planned "fix once,
  close many" groups, so that work reuses this catalogue.
- Custom step catalogues for users and packs.
- Measured user impact from sign-in logs and report-only results. It would add measures later.
- Goals for GitHub, Azure DevOps and Active Directory. Until they exist, those runs look as they do today.
- A model that decides pass, fail, severity or order. Order comes from the catalogue, and every relationship
  cites its source.

content.content:
## 11. Measures

17 of the 43 steps in the first catalogue have no Maester check (section 15). Two of them are tenant states that
a figure from Graph settles, so in Phase 1 they get measures, not tests. The owner ruled on 5 November 2026 that
readiness is a data point, not a test. A share of compliant devices isn't a misconfiguration and has no meaningful
severity or ATT&CK technique, so it must not change pass rates or the test count. A measure also runs whenever its
step is in scope, so "Before you fix this" shows a real figure even after a one-test run, where a test would have
had to be selected.

A measure is an entry in the measure registry, `powershell/assets/MaesterMeasures.psd1`:

```powershell
@{
    Measures = @(
        @{
            Key         = 'devices-compliant'
            Function    = 'Get-MtDeviceComplianceShare'
            Title       = 'Devices that sign in are compliant'
            Unit        = 'devices'
            Service     = 'Graph'
            License     = 'INTUNE_A'
            Permission  = 'Graph:Scope:Device.Read.All'
        }
    )
}
```

- `Service`, `License` and `Permission` use the grammar of the test attributes, and the engine applies them the
  way it gates a test. A measure whose gate fails is Unknown with the matching reason code.
- `Function` names an internal reader in `powershell/internal/services/<service>/`. It reads through the Graph
  cache and returns `Count` (the objects that meet the bar), `Total`, and `Objects` (those that fall short, as
  `Type`, `Id` and `DisplayName`). The engine keeps up to 100 of them.
- The engine works out `Share`, compares it with the step's `MinimumShare` or the run config's override, and
  writes the result to the step (section 7.2).
- Readers write object facts with the shared keys (section 12) for the objects they list.

| Key | Step | Reads | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Entra `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | The objects are the devices a compliant-device policy would block. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so |
| `mfa-registered` | `entra.mfa-registered` | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` for enabled member users | Needs Entra ID P1. Leaves out the emergency access accounts |

Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
see the devices that have no identity yet. The emergency access accounts holding Global Administrator as a
permanent active assignment is another state with no Maester check.

The Defender–Intune connector is not covered. MT.1098 checks the health of the Mobile Threat Defense connectors it
finds, and skips or passes when the Defender connector is missing. The `defender-device-risk` goal needs four
checks before Maester can follow it: the Defender connector is enabled, its compliance toggle is on for each
platform that has a compliance policy, and Windows and Android Enterprise compliance policies require a machine
risk score.

A measure isn't a test: it has no ID, no row in `Tests` and no attribute review, and it plays no part in pass
rates, frameworks or the test count. Packs can't add measures in Phase 1.

## 12. Object facts
## 16. Delivery

| Milestone | Work | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 Format | Schema and loader (`Get-MtStepCatalog`, internal), the `Step` attribute in C#, the schema table and the reader, `StepCatalog.Tests.ps1`, and the compliant-devices goal as the fixture | This design |
| M2 Catalogue | Expert pass on the seven goals against the mirrors, then `Step` on about 75 tests, plus `Step` in the Zero Trust `taxonomy.json` | M1, and the instance-attribute change on `feat/zta-taxonomy-mapping` |
| M3 Engine | `Step` on rows, reading the measures of the steps in scope, `Get-MtResultStep` (status, readiness, rank, scope), `LastKnown`, `-Step`, `-IncludePrerequisites`, `Get-MtTest -Step`, CSV and Markdown columns, the console line | M1 |
| M4 Report | Action plan groups and lanes, Before you fix this, rollout in How to fix, the overview card | M3's result shape. It can start on sample data once section 7 is final |
| M5 Measures | The measure registry, the two readers of section 11, and `Measure` on their steps | M1 for the format. The readers can be written before it |
| M6 Tooling | `build/steps/` scripts and the weekly workflow | M1 |
| M7 Docs and site | `Step` in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`, a defender's path page, and one page per goal on maester.dev built by `prepare-data.mjs` | M2 |

Once M1 lands, M2, M5 and M6 touch different files and can run in parallel sessions. M3 and M4 follow in order.

## 17. Decisions

The owner accepted the recommended answer to each decision on 5 November 2026, and changed decision 10 later that day.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `devices-compliant` | `intune.devices-compliant` | Entra `devices` that signed in within 30 days, by `isManaged` and `isCompliant` | The objects are the devices a compliant-device policy would block. Devices with no Entra identity can't be seen, and the result says so |
| `mfa-registered` | `entra.mfa-registered` | `reports/authenticationMethods/userRegistrationDetails` for enabled member users | Needs Entra ID P1. Leaves out the emergency access accounts |

Later: phishing-resistant method registration for all users (ZTA.21782 covers privileged users only),
password writeback once a Graph API reports it, security defaults being off in tenants licensed for
Conditional Access (section 15), and hybrid join and Windows device registration, which need sign-in data to
see the devices that have no identity yet. The emergency access accounts holding Global Administrator as a
permanent active assignment is another state with no Maester check.

The Defender–Intune connector is not covered. MT.1098 checks the health of the Mobile Threat Defense connectors it
finds, and skips or passes when the Defender connector is missing. The `defender-device-risk` goal needs four
checks before Maester can follow it: the Defender connector is enabled, its compliance toggle is on for each
platform that has a compliance policy, and Windows and Android Enterprise compliance policies require a machine
risk score.

A measure isn't a test: it has no ID, no row in `Tests` and no attribute review, and it plays no part in pass
rates, frameworks or the test count. Packs can't add measures in Phase 1.

## 12. Object facts
## 16. Delivery

| Milestone | Work | Needs |

| M4 Report | Action plan groups and lanes, Before you fix this, rollout in How to fix, the overview card | M3's result shape. It can start on sample data once section 7 is final |
| M5 Measures | The measure registry, the two readers of section 11, and `Measure` on their steps | M1 for the format. The readers can be written before it |
| M6 Tooling | `build/steps/` scripts and the weekly workflow | M1 |

content.content:
﻿param (
    $TestGeneral = $true,

    $TestFunctions = $true,

    [ValidateSet('None', 'Normal', 'Detailed', 'Diagnostic')]
    [Alias('Show')]
    $Output = "None",

    # File name patterns to run, for example 'Get-MtUser*' or 'RepositoryLayout*', 'Help*'.
    [string[]]
    $Include = "*",

    # File name patterns to skip, for example 'Golden*', 'GeneratedFileFormatting*'.
    [string[]]
    $Exclude = "",

    [switch]
    $NoError,

    # When set (or when $env:PESTER_COVERAGE equals 'true'), runs all tests in a single combined Pester invocation and generates a JaCoCo code-coverage report.
    [switch]
    $Coverage,

    # How many pwsh processes run test files at the same time. The default is 2 (1 on a single-core machine):
    # each process needs up to about 1.3 GB of memory, and 4 at once peaked at about 4.4 GB. On a machine with
    # memory to spare, -ThrottleLimit 4 runs the suite in about half the time.
    [ValidateRange(1, 64)]
    [int]
    $ThrottleLimit = [Math]::Min(2, [Environment]::ProcessorCount),

    # How many test files each pwsh process runs before it exits and frees its memory.
    [ValidateRange(1, 1000)]
    [int]
    $FilesPerProcess = 8,

    # Runs every test file in this process, as pester.ps1 used to. Useful when debugging a test,
    # but each file that re-imports the module keeps another copy of it in memory (about 60 MB each).
    [switch]
    $InProcess,

    # When set (or when $env:PESTER_SKIP_OS_INDEPENDENT equals 'true'), skips the tests whose result does not depend
    # on the operating system: the general tests that only read files (lint, formatting, ScriptAnalyzer, help,
    # generator drift) and the golden fixtures. CI runs them on the Linux leg only.
    [switch]
    $SkipOsIndependent,

    # When set (or when $env:PESTER_SKIP_GOLDEN equals 'true'), skips the Maester 2.x golden fixtures. CI sets it on
    # a pull request that changes none of their inputs.
    [switch]
    $SkipGolden
)

Write-Host "Starting Tests"
# Unit tests never send telemetry; the worker processes inherit this.
$env:MAESTER_DISABLE_TELEMETRY = '1'

Write-Host "Importing Module"

Remove-Module Maester -ErrorAction Ignore

input.command:
git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(engine): put the measures on their steps, with the owner's rulings

- intune.devices-compliant and entra.mfa-registered name their measures
  (MinimumShare 95) and lose their Unchecked text.
- devices-compliant declares INTUNE_A: only Intune marks devices
  compliant, and a compliance partner's devices need Intune licences too.
- A registry entry may carry a Caveat, one line on what the figure
  can't see. Both measures have one.
- The MFA measure counts isMfaCapable, so a method the authentication
  methods policy no longer allows doesn't count. It is now mfa-capable,
  read by Get-MtMfaCapableShare.
- The design doc records the rulings, and notes that readers write
  object facts only once M3 lists a measure's objects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -5 && git push origin feat/defenders-path 2>&1 | tail -3

I merged all three branches into `feat/defenders-path` with your three rulings and pushed to draft PR [maester365/maester#2683](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2683). All 6,972 unit tests pass and the module build passes. I left out the Zero Trust test that starts a real assessment. CI on the new push hasn't reported yet.

**Your three rulings**
1. **Intune licence:** the device measure now requires Intune (`INTUNE_A`). A tenant without Intune gets Unknown with the licence reason, not "0 of N compliant". The design doc records your reason: only Intune marks devices compliant, and a compliance partner's devices need Intune licences too.
2. **Caveat:** each measure can now carry one line, up to 200 characters, on what its figure can't count. The report will show it next to the figure.
   - Devices: devices that aren't registered or joined in Entra can't be counted.
   - MFA: only methods the policy allows count, and guests, disabled users, emergency access and sync accounts are left out.
3. **MFA:** the measure now uses `isMfaCapable`, so a user whose only method is one the policy no longer allows doesn't count. I renamed it to `mfa-capable` and its reader to `Get-MtMfaCapableShare`. The step keeps its ID, `entra.mfa-registered`.

**The merge**
- Both readiness steps now name their measure at 95%, and their `Unchecked` lines are gone. That leaves 15 of the 43 steps with no Maester check.
- The design doc conflicted where M2 still described readiness as tests. I kept the measures wording and used M2's catalogue table, with the two measures in place of "readiness check".

**Two things for later**
- **Facts:** the readers can't add object facts usefully yet. Facts only attach to objects that the run already lists, so they have to wait until M3 shows a measure's objects on the Affected objects page.
- **Fact key:** the shared key `user.mfaRegistered` doesn't mean "can complete MFA", so M3 will need a new `user.mfaCapable` key.

The defender's path puts fixes in the order Microsoft Learn documents: what has to be in place before a fix works, what a fix unlocks, and whether the tenant is ready for it. Attack-path tools show the route an attacker takes. None of them show the order a defender has to work in.

All 15 decisions in section 17 were accepted on 5 November 2026.
2. **Milestone 1: the format and the attribute.**
   - `Step` on `[MaesterTest]`: the C# class, the schema table and the reader. Values are stored in lowercase, with at most three per test. The engine DLL is rebuilt, and `Build-MaesterEngine.ps1 -Verify` passes.

- Object facts gained `Key` and `Raw` in #2681. Section 12 of the design lists the keys this design reads.

## Tests

- New: `powershell/tests/functions/engine/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1` (27 tests, with fixtures for each catalogue problem and the reader rules) and `powershell/tests/general/StepCatalog.Tests.ps1` (the shipped catalogue, schema validation, goal order).
