## Quick start

Prefer to click through the choices? The [test builder](/test-builder) explains every attribute and
writes the code for you.

```powershell
# 1. Create custom/Test.CONTOSO.1001.ps1 and custom/Test.CONTOSO.1001.md
New-MtTest -Id CONTOSO.1001 -Title 'Guest invitations are restricted' -Service Graph -Severity High `
    -Product entra -Feature external-identities -Area external-access

# 2. Edit the two files, then check them. No tenant connection is needed for this step.
Get-MtTest -Path ./custom

# 3. Run the test on its own while you write it
Connect-Maester
Invoke-MtTest -Path ./custom/Test.CONTOSO.1001.ps1

# 4. Run it with everything else
Invoke-Maester -Path .
```

`New-MtTest` writes to `./custom` unless you pass `-Path`. It supports `-WhatIf` and refuses to overwrite
existing files unless you pass `-Force`. Only `-Id` and `-Title` are required; `-Product`, `-Feature`, `-Area`,
`-ResourceType`, `-UserImpact`, `-ImplementationCost` and `-Mitre` fill in the attributes of the same name.

## Files and layout

Put your tests in a folder of your own, usually `custom/` inside the folder you run Maester from:

```text
maester/
  maester-config.json        (optional: your run configuration)
  custom/
    Test.CONTOSO.1001.ps1
    Test.CONTOSO.1001.md
    suite.json               (optional: name, tags and source for every test in the folder)
    maester-config.json      (optional: an overlay on the root config)
```

`Invoke-Maester -Path ./maester` finds every `Test.*.ps1` file under the path, in any subfolder up to three
levels deep (`./maester/a/b/c/Test.CONTOSO.1001.ps1`). If you leave out `-Path`, Maester looks for custom
tests only in the `custom` folder of the current folder, and reads the config files of the current folder. Without
a `custom` folder only the built-in tests run.

Pester-format tests (`*.Tests.ps1`) must be in a `custom` folder: `-Path` itself, or a `custom` folder under it.
See [Pester-format tests](./pester-format-tests.md).

Maester matches the `custom` folder name without regard to case, so a `Custom` folder created by Maester 2.x keeps
working, and `New-MtTest` writes into it when it exists.

Rules for a test file:

- The file name is `Test.<ID>.ps1`, where `<ID>` is the `Id` in the attribute. The `.md` file has the same
  name with the `.md` extension and sits in the same folder. A custom test without its `.md` file is reported
  as `Error` with reason `InvalidMetadata`.
- The file contains exactly one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute. It may contain other functions
  (helpers, or a family's instance source).
- At the top level the file contains only function definitions: no statements, no script-level `param()`
  block. Discovery never executes the file, and this rule keeps it that way.
- The test function has `[CmdletBinding()]`.

### Test IDs

An ID is letters and digits in segments separated by `.` or `-` (and `_` after the first segment). It starts
with a letter, contains at least one digit or separator, and is at most 64 characters. `CONTOSO.1001`,
`CONTOSO-ID-07` and `CT0001` are all valid. IDs are compared case-insensitively.

A test that implements a benchmark requirement is named after it: the suite's prefix, then the requirement's
ID as the benchmark writes it, without a version suffix. That is also its `Id` in the framework file. The prefix ends in a period;
the rest keeps the benchmark's own punctuation, so a reader can search for the ID the benchmark uses.

| Test ID | Prefix | The benchmark's ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CIS.M365.5.2.2.2` | `CIS.M365.` | Recommendation `5.2.2.2` of the CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark |
| `CISA.MS.AAD.3.1` | `CISA.` | SCuBA policy `MS.AAD.3.1v1`, without its version suffix |
| `ASD.ISM-1504` | `ASD.` | ISM control `ISM-1504`, written with a hyphen by ASD |

Use a prefix of your own. These prefixes belong to the tests that ship with Maester: `MT.`, `CISA.`, `CIS.`,
`EIDSCA.`, `ORCA.`, `AD-`, `AZDO.`, `ASD.` and `MT1060.`. `MP.` is reserved for Maester Packs, third-party test packs
planned for a later release. A custom test with one of these prefixes still runs, with a
warning. A custom test that uses the exact ID of a built-in test is not run at all, and the built-in runs
instead. To change how a built-in test behaves, set its parameters or severity in the
[run configuration](../configuration/run-configuration.md), or copy it under your own ID and disable the
built-in.

Two native tests with the same ID (or the same function name) both get an `Error` row with reason
`DuplicateId`, and neither runs. When a native test and a Pester-format test share an ID, the native test
runs and the Pester test does not; it is listed under `Selection.Superseded` in the result with `MatchedBy`
`NativeTest`.

## A complete example

`custom/Test.CONTOSO.1002.ps1`:

```powershell
function Test-ContosoDisabledCaPolicyReason {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id           = 'CONTOSO.1002',
        Title        = 'Disabled Conditional Access policies state why they are disabled.',
        Product      = 'entra',
        Feature      = 'conditional-access',
        Area         = 'access-control',
        ResourceType = 'ConditionalAccessPolicy',
        Severity     = 'Medium',
        Service      = 'Graph',
        License      = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Tag          = 'Contoso'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # Text that a disabled policy's name must contain.
        [string] $ReasonMarker = 'Disabled:'
    )

    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy
    $withoutReason = @($policies | Where-Object { $_.state -eq 'disabled' -and $_.displayName -notlike "*$ReasonMarker*" })

    if ($withoutReason.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Well done. Every disabled policy states why it is disabled.'
        return $true
    }

    $result = "These disabled policies do not state why they are disabled:`n`n%TestResult%"
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $result -GraphObjects $withoutReason -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
    return $false
}
```

`custom/Test.CONTOSO.1002.md`:

```md
Disabled Conditional Access policies must say why they are disabled, in the form `Disabled: <reason>`.

#### Remediation action

1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open **Protection** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**.
2. For each policy listed below, add the reason to its name, or delete the policy.

#### Related links

- [Conditional Access policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies)

<!--- Results --->
%TestResult%
```

There is no connection check, no licence check and no `try`/`catch` in the function. The engine does all three.

## The `[MaesterTest]` attribute
## What the function returns

| The function does | Result | Reason code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| returns `$true` | `Passed` | |
| returns `$false` | `Failed` | |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate` | `Investigate`, whatever it returns | |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause <code>` | `Skipped`. The call ends the test. | `TestSkipped`, or `NotApplicable` for `-SkippedBecause NotApplicable` |
| calls `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Error`, or throws any error | `Error` | `TestError` |
| returns `$null` without skipping or `-Investigate` | `Skipped` | `NoResult` |
| returns something that is not a boolean, or more than one value | `Error` | `InvalidReturn` |
| runs longer than the configured timeout | `Error` | `Timeout` |

When several apply, they are evaluated in this order: `-SkippedBecause Error`, `-Investigate`, any other
skip, an uncaught error, the returned value.

Watch for stray output. A command whose output you do not capture (`$list.Add($x)` on an `ArrayList`, for
example) adds a second value to the function's output and turns the result into `InvalidReturn`. Assign such
calls to `$null` or pipe them to `Out-Null`.

### Add-MtTestResultDetail

[`Add-MtTestResultDetail`](../commands/Add-MtTestResultDetail.mdx) works as in 2.x. The parameters you use in a
native test:

- `-Result`: the Markdown result. It replaces `%TestResult%` in the `.md` file.
- `-GraphObjects` and `-GraphObjectType`: a list of objects rendered as a table with links to the admin
  portal, inserted where `%TestResult%` appears in `-Result`. See
  [Formatting test results](./formatting-test-results.md).
- `-Investigate`: the result needs a person to look at it.
- `-SkippedBecause`: skip the test for a reason only the test can see, such as `NotApplicable`,
  `NotSupportedAppPermission` or `Custom` with `-SkippedCustomReason`. Do not use the `NotConnected*` and
  `NotLicensed*` codes for conditions the attribute can declare; use `Service` and `License`.
- `-Description`: replaces the description from the `.md` file. Leave it out to use the `.md`.

`-TestTitle` and `-Severity` are ignored in a single-result native test: the title and severity come from the
attribute and the config. In a family, `-TestTitle` sets the instance's title when the instance object has no
`Title`. `-Severity` is used only when neither the config nor the attribute sets one.

### Embedding another tool's report

A test or a family's instance source that runs another tool can embed that tool's own single-file HTML report in
the Maester report with `Add-MtReportAttachment`:

```powershell
Add-MtReportAttachment -Name 'Zero Trust Assessment' -Path "$outputPath/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html"
```

The report lists it near the bottom of the left menu (a pack's test's report goes in that pack's menu instead), and shows a button with that name on its overview page and
on the test's result (on every instance of a family). Each opens the embedded report in the main panel, beside the
Maester navigation, with a link to open it in a new browser tab. The attached report runs in a sandboxed frame
without access to the Maester report or its data. It works offline, so the Maester report stays one
file to share. The file is read and compressed at once, so you can delete the tool's output folder afterwards. The JSON
results file lists the attachment's name and size, not its content, and the HTML report leaves HTML attachments out
when `-RedactUserIdentity` is used.

With `-ContentType application/json`, an attachment is data for a view built into the report, which finds it by
its `Name` (the Zero Trust Assessment pack attaches its Zero Trust plan as `zero-trust-workshop`). It is not shown
as a button, and under `-RedactUserIdentity` it is redacted like the results instead of being left out.

### Errors and skips

Do not wrap the body in `try`/`catch` only to report `-SkippedBecause Error`. The engine runs every test inside
its own `try`, so any terminating error ends the test and becomes an `Error` row with the exception message as
`ReasonDetail` and the error record in `ErrorRecord`. Statement-terminating errors (a failed command, a method
call on `$null`) also end the test, so it cannot carry on with empty data and return `$true` by accident.

You may still use `try`/`catch` for a condition you handle, for example a 403 from Graph that you report as
`-SkippedBecause NotAuthorized`. A `-SkippedBecause` call made inside your own `try` block still skips the
test; the engine recognises the skip when your `catch` passes it to `Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause
Error -SkippedError $_`.

Warnings and non-terminating errors written by the test are shown on the console and stored on the result row
in `Diagnostics`.

## Declare what the test needs

Do not check connections or licences in the test. Declare them, and the engine decides before the test runs.
A test whose requirement is not met gets a `Skipped` row with a reason code and its `.md` description, so it
still appears in the report. See [Applicability](../configuration/applicability.md) for the order of the
checks and every reason code.

## Families: one test, several results

`InstanceSource` with the name of a function in the same file. The engine calls that function when the test
runs (never during discovery) and runs the test once per object it returns, passing the object as `$Instance`.

```powershell
function Get-ContosoAdminUnit {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    foreach ($unit in Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'directory/administrativeUnits') {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Id    = $unit.id                     # required: the instance suffix
            Title = "Administrative unit '$($unit.displayName)' is restricted"   # optional
            Data  = $unit                        # optional: anything the test needs
        }
    }
}

function Test-ContosoAdminUnitRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CONTOSO.2001',
        Title = 'Administrative units are restricted.',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        Service = 'Graph',
        InstanceSource = 'Get-ContosoAdminUnit'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param(
        # The administrative unit to check, supplied by the engine.
        $Instance
    )

    $restricted = [bool]$Instance.Data.isMemberManagementRestricted
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Member management restricted: $restricted"
    return $restricted
```
```json
}
```

A `suite.json` in a test folder sets what is true for every test in it (and its subfolders, unless a nearer
`suite.json` exists):

```json

  "Id": "Contoso",

  "Source": "Custom",

  "HelpUrlTemplate": "https://wiki.contoso.com/maester/{Id}",

}
```

| --- | --- |

function Test-PoraGuestInviteRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'PORA.1001', Title = 'Only admins and guest inviters can invite guests',
        Product = 'entra', Feature = 'external-identities', Area = 'external-access', ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High', Service = 'Graph'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
    $policy = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'policies/authorizationPolicy'
    $allowed = @($policy)[0].allowInvitesFrom
    $ok = $allowed -in 'adminsAndGuestInviters', 'none'
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Guest invitations are allowed from: **$allowed**."
    return $ok
}
EOF

#### Remediation action

1. In the Microsoft Entra admin center, open **External Identities** > **External collaboration settings**.
2. Under **Guest invite settings**, select **Only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite guest users**.

%TestResult%
EOF

w PORA.1002 <<'EOF'
function Test-PoraDisabledCaPolicyReason {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'PORA.1002', Title = 'Disabled Conditional Access policies state why they are disabled',
        Product = 'entra', Feature = 'conditional-access', Area = 'access-control', ResourceType = 'ConditionalAccessPolicy',
        Severity = 'Medium', Service = 'Graph', License = 'AAD_PREMIUM'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param([string] $ReasonMarker = 'Disabled:')

        return $true

    return $false
}

%TestResult%
EOF

function Test-PoraGuestInviteRestricted {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'PORA.1001', Title = 'Only admins and guest inviters can invite guests',
        Product = 'entra', Feature = 'external-identities', Area = 'external-access', ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High', Service = 'Graph'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
    $policy = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'policies/authorizationPolicy'
    $allowed = @($policy)[0].allowInvitesFrom

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Guest invitations are allowed from: **$allowed**."
    return $ok
}

m PORA.1001 <<'EOF'
Only administrators and users in the Guest Inviter role should be able to invite guests.

w PORA.1002 <<'EOF'
function Test-PoraDisabledCaPolicyReason {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'PORA.1002', Title = 'Disabled Conditional Access policies state why they are disabled',
        Product = 'entra', Feature = 'conditional-access', Area = 'access-control', ResourceType = 'ConditionalAccessPolicy',
        Severity = 'Medium', Service = 'Graph', License = 'AAD_PREMIUM'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param([string] $ReasonMarker = 'Disabled:')
    $withoutReason = @(Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object { $_.state -eq 'disabled' -and $_.displayName -notlike "*$ReasonMarker*" })
    if ($withoutReason.Count -eq 0) {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Well done. Every disabled policy states why it is disabled.'
        return $true
    }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "These disabled policies do not state why they are disabled:`n`n%TestResult%" -GraphObjects $withoutReason -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess
    return $false
}
EOF
m PORA.1002 <<'EOF'
Disabled Conditional Access policies must say why they are disabled, in the form `Disabled: <reason>`.

#### Remediation action

function Test-PoraGlobalAdminCount {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'PORA.1003', Title = 'The tenant has between two and four Global Administrators',
        Product = 'entra', Feature = 'roles', Area = 'privileged-access', ResourceType = 'DirectoryRole',
        Severity = 'Critical', Service = 'Graph'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param([int] $Minimum = 2, [int] $Maximum = 4)
    $members = @(Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "directoryRoles(roleTemplateId='62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10')/members")
    $count = $members.Count
    $text = "The tenant has **$count** Global Administrators. The range is $Minimum to $Maximum.`n`n%TestResult%"

    return ($count -ge $Minimum -and $count -le $Maximum)
}
EOF

content.text:
I wrote 10 custom tests in [scratch/custom](scratch/custom) and checked them with `Get-MtTest -Path`. I only ran them without a tenant connection: that run made a working report with no console errors. The Graph checks haven't run against Pora yet. Git ignores `scratch/` through this worktree's local exclude file, so the folder never shows up as a change.

They're chosen to give the report a mix of results:

| Test | What it checks | Without a connection | Connected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PORA.1001 | Who can invite guests | Skipped | Pass or fail |
| PORA.1002 | Disabled CA policies state why | Skipped | Pass or fail, with a policy table |
| PORA.1003 | 2–4 Global Admins | Skipped | Pass or fail, with a user table |
| PORA.1004 | Security defaults vs CA | Skipped | Investigate if defaults are on |
| PORA.1005 | Each enabled CA policy excludes break-glass | Skipped | One row per policy (a family) |
| PORA.1006 | Custom domains verified | Skipped | Markdown table of domains |
| PORA.1007 | Teams guest calling | Skipped | Skipped unless Teams is connected |
| PORA.1008 | Runbook owner (needs no tenant) | Passed | Passed |
| PORA.1009 | Directory sync server | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| PORA.1010 | Threat feed file | Error (on purpose) | Error |

They spread across the Entra, Teams and Defender products, plus one test with no product, so the Products menu has a few groups.

To run them, first build and load the module with the new report template:

```bash
cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/zero-trust-view && pwsh -NoExit -c "./build/Build-LocalMaester.ps1 -BuildReport"
```

Then, in that PowerShell window, connect and run only the custom tests:

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Path ./scratch/custom -SkipBuiltIn -OutputFolder ./scratch/results
```

The report opens when the run ends and is saved in `scratch/results`. To see Maester's built-in tests too, leave out `-SkipBuiltIn`. To add the Zero Trust pack's results, add `-Pack ZTA`; that starts the full assessment and takes much longer.

`Build-LocalMaester.ps1 -BuildReport` rewrites `powershell/assets/ReportTemplate.html`. That's fine locally, but don't commit it.

$7
}

$8

#### Remediation action

$9

t DEMO.2001 Test-DemoMfaCoverage 'At least 95% of users are registered for MFA' \
  "Product = 'entra', Feature = 'authentication-methods', Area = 'authentication', ResourceType = 'User'," High '[int] $Target = 95' \
'    $registered = 412; $total = 448
    $pct = [math]::Round($registered / $total * 100, 1)
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "**$registered** of **$total** users ($pct%) are registered for MFA. The target is $Target%."
    return ($pct -ge $Target)' \
'Users without a registered MFA method can be phished with a password alone. (Demo data.)' \
'Run a registration campaign from **Protection** > **Authentication methods** > **Registration campaign**.'

t DEMO.2002 Test-DemoLegacyAuthBlocked 'Legacy authentication is blocked' \
  "Product = 'entra', Feature = 'conditional-access', Area = 'authentication', ResourceType = 'ConditionalAccessPolicy'," Critical '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "A Conditional Access policy named **Block legacy authentication** is on and covers all users."
    return $true' \
'Legacy protocols such as IMAP and POP cannot do MFA. (Demo data.)' \
'Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks the **Exchange ActiveSync clients** and **Other clients** client apps.'

t DEMO.2003 Test-DemoStaleGuests 'No guest has been inactive for more than 90 days' \
  "Product = 'entra', Feature = 'external-identities', Area = 'external-access', ResourceType = 'User'," Medium '[int] $Days = 90' \
'    $guests = @(
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = "alex@fabrikam.com"; LastSignIn = "2026-03-02" }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = "sam@northwind.com"; LastSignIn = "2026-05-19" }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = "jo@tailspin.com"; LastSignIn = "Never" }
    )
    $rows = $guests | ForEach-Object { "| $($_.Name) | $($_.LastSignIn) |" }
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result ("These guests have not signed in for more than $Days days:`n`n| Guest | Last sign-in |`n| --- | --- |`n" + ($rows -join "`n"))
    return $false' \
'Guests who no longer work with you keep their access until someone removes them. (Demo data.)' \
'Set up an access review for guests in **Identity Governance** > **Access reviews**.'

t DEMO.2004 Test-DemoBreakGlassSignIn 'Emergency access accounts were not used in the last 30 days' \
  "Product = 'entra', Feature = 'roles', Area = 'privileged-access', ResourceType = 'User'," High '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate -Result "**bg-admin-01@pora.example** signed in on 2026-10-28 from 203.0.113.24. Check that this was a planned test."
    return $false' \
'Any sign-in by an emergency access account should be explained. (Demo data.)' \
'Review the sign-in in **Monitoring** > **Sign-in logs** and record why it happened.'

t DEMO.2005 Test-DemoMailboxAuditing 'Mailbox auditing is on for every mailbox' \
  "Product = 'exchange', Area = 'logging-and-detection', ResourceType = 'Mailbox'," Medium '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Auditing is on for all **1,284** mailboxes."
    return $true' \
'Mailbox audit logs show who read or changed mail. (Demo data.)' \
'Run `Set-OrganizationConfig -AuditDisabled $false`.'

t DEMO.2006 Test-DemoExternalForwarding 'Mail is not forwarded automatically to outside domains' \
  "Product = 'exchange', Area = 'email-protection', ResourceType = 'MailFlowRule'," High '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Two inbox rules forward mail outside the tenant:`n`n| Mailbox | Forwards to |`n| --- | --- |`n| finance@pora.example | invoices@gmail.example |`n| ceo-office@pora.example | archive@outlook.example |"
    return $false' \
'Automatic forwarding is a common way to steal mail after an account is compromised. (Demo data.)' \
'Set the outbound spam policy''s **Automatic forwarding rules** to **Off**.'

t DEMO.2007 Test-DemoSharingLinks 'Default sharing links are scoped to specific people' \
  "Product = 'sharepoint', Area = 'data-protection', ResourceType = 'Tenant'," Medium '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "The default link type is **People in your organization**. Consider **Specific people**."
    return $false' \
'Links that work for everyone in the organisation are often forwarded further than intended. (Demo data.)' \
'In the SharePoint admin center, open **Policies** > **Sharing** and set **File and folder links** to **Specific people**.'

t DEMO.2008 Test-DemoTeamsAnonymousJoin 'Anonymous users cannot join Teams meetings' \
  "Product = 'teams', Area = 'external-access', ResourceType = 'Tenant'," Low '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Anonymous users can join meetings, but they wait in the lobby."
    return $true' \
'Anonymous joins let anyone with the link into a meeting. (Demo data.)' \
'In the Teams admin center, set **Anonymous users can join a meeting** to **Off**.'

t DEMO.2009 Test-DemoDefenderTamper 'Tamper protection is on for every device' \
  "Product = 'defender', Area = 'devices', ResourceType = 'Device'," High '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause Custom -SkippedCustomReason "Device data was not exported for this demo."' \
'Tamper protection stops malware from turning Defender off. (Demo data.)' \
'Turn on **Tamper protection** in **Settings** > **Endpoints** > **Advanced features**.'

t DEMO.2010 Test-DemoIntuneCompliance 'Devices are marked non-compliant when no policy applies' \
  "Product = 'intune', Area = 'devices', ResourceType = 'Device'," Medium '' \
'    throw "Could not read the compliance settings export: the file is empty."' \
'A device with no compliance policy should not count as compliant. (Demo data; this test errors on purpose.)' \
'In Intune, open **Devices** > **Compliance** > **Compliance settings** and set **Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as** to **Not compliant**.'

function Get-DemoAdminAccount {
    [CmdletBinding()]
    param()
    @(
        @{ Id = 'adele'; Name = 'Adele Vance'; Phish = $true; Role = 'Global Administrator' }
        @{ Id = 'megan'; Name = 'Megan Bowen'; Phish = $true; Role = 'Security Administrator' }
        @{ Id = 'lee'; Name = 'Lee Gu'; Phish = $false; Role = 'Exchange Administrator' }
        @{ Id = 'nestor'; Name = 'Nestor Wilke'; Phish = $false; Role = 'Global Administrator' }
        @{ Id = 'pradeep'; Name = 'Pradeep Gupta'; Phish = $true; Role = 'User Administrator' }
    ) | ForEach-Object {
        [pscustomobject]@{ Id = $_.Id; Title = "$($_.Name) uses a phishing-resistant sign-in method"; Fields = @{ Role = $_.Role }; Data = $_ }
    }
}

function Test-DemoAdminPhishResistant {
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'DEMO.2011', Title = 'Administrators use phishing-resistant sign-in methods',
        Product = 'entra', Feature = 'authentication-methods', Area = 'privileged-access', ResourceType = 'User',
        Severity = 'Critical', InstanceSource = 'Get-DemoAdminAccount'

    [OutputType([bool])]

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "**$($Instance.Data.Name)** ($($Instance.Data.Role)) signs in with $method."
    return [bool]$Instance.Data.Phish
}
EOF

%TestResult%
EOF

  "Product = 'exchange', Area = 'logging-and-detection', ResourceType = 'Mailbox'," Medium '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Auditing is on for all **1,284** mailboxes."
    return $true' \
'Mailbox audit logs show who read or changed mail. (Demo data.)' \
'Run `Set-OrganizationConfig -AuditDisabled $false`.'

t DEMO.2006 Test-DemoExternalForwarding 'Mail is not forwarded automatically to outside domains' \
  "Product = 'exchange', Area = 'email-protection', ResourceType = 'MailFlowRule'," High '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "Two inbox rules forward mail outside the tenant:`n`n| Mailbox | Forwards to |`n| --- | --- |`n| finance@pora.example | invoices@gmail.example |`n| ceo-office@pora.example | archive@outlook.example |"
    return $false' \
'Automatic forwarding is a common way to steal mail after an account is compromised. (Demo data.)' \
'Set the outbound spam policy''s **Automatic forwarding rules** to **Off**.'

t DEMO.2007 Test-DemoSharingLinks 'Default sharing links are scoped to specific people' \
  "Product = 'sharepoint', Area = 'data-protection', ResourceType = 'Tenant'," Medium '' \
'    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result "The default link type is **People in your organization**. Consider **Specific people**."
    return $false' \

I wrote 12 tests in [scratch/local](scratch/local) that need no tenant: each returns made-up demo data. I ran them, and the report shows no console errors. That report is [scratch/results-local/TestResults-2026-11-07-233107.html](scratch/results-local/TestResults-2026-11-07-233107.html).

| Test | Product | Severity | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DEMO.2001 MFA registration ≥ 95% | Entra | High | Failed (92%) |
| DEMO.2002 Legacy auth blocked | Entra | Critical | Passed |
| DEMO.2003 No stale guests | Entra | Medium | Failed, with a guest table |
| DEMO.2004 Break-glass not used | Entra | High | Investigate |
| DEMO.2005 Mailbox auditing on | Exchange | Medium | Passed |
| DEMO.2006 No external forwarding | Exchange | High | Failed, with a mailbox table |
| DEMO.2007 Sharing links scoped | SharePoint | Medium | Failed |
| DEMO.2008 Anonymous Teams join | Teams | Low | Passed |
| DEMO.2009 Tamper protection | Defender | High | Skipped (custom reason) |
| DEMO.2010 Intune compliance default | Intune | Medium | Error (on purpose) |
| DEMO.2011 Admins phishing-resistant | Entra | Critical | Family of 5: 3 passed, 2 failed |
| DEMO.2012 Passwords never expire | Entra | Low | Passed |

In all, 16 results: 7 passed, 6 failed, 1 to investigate, 1 skipped and 1 error. That's enough for the action plan, the severity breakdown and the Products menu to have content. Each admin in the DEMO.2011 family also carries a `Role` field.

To run them yourself, build and load the module, then run only these tests without connecting:

```bash
cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/zero-trust-view && pwsh -NoExit -c "./build/Build-LocalMaester.ps1 -BuildReport"
```

```powershell
Invoke-Maester -Path ./scratch/local -SkipBuiltIn -SkipGraphConnect -OutputFolder ./scratch/results-local
```

To see both demo sets in one report, use `-Path ./scratch`. The Graph tests in `scratch/custom` are then skipped unless you run `Connect-Maester` first.

  printf '%s. (Demo data.)\n\n<!--- Results --->\n%%TestResult%%\n' "$title" > ad/Test.$id.md

cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/zero-trust-view/scratch; mkdir -p bare ad
# Bare: only Id and Title
i=0
for spec in "Backup job finished in the last 24 hours|true" "Release branch is protected|true" "Build agents run the latest image|false" "Vendor contract register is up to date|false" "Firewall change log was reviewed this week|investigate" "Office printers have current firmware|true" "Staging certificates expire in more than 30 days|false" "Old VPN profiles are removed|skip"; do
  i=$((i+1)); title="${spec%|*}"; r="${spec#*|}"; id="CHK.$((300+i))"
  case $r in
    true) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Looks good.'
    return \$true";;
    false) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'This did not meet the bar.'
    return \$false";;
    investigate) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate -Result 'Someone should look at this.'
    return \$false";;
    skip) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause NotApplicable";;
  esac
  cat > bare/Test.$id.ps1 <<EOF
function Test-Chk$((300+i)) {
    [MaesterTest(Id = '$id', Title = '$title')]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
$body
}
EOF
  printf '%s\n\n<!--- Results --->\n%%TestResult%%\n' "$title." > bare/Test.$id.md
done
# AD-like: Product ad, no Service so they run without a domain
cat > ad/suite.json <<'EOF'
{ "Id": "ContosoAD", "Name": "Contoso Active Directory checks", "Source": "Custom" }
EOF
j=0
for spec in "The KRBTGT password was changed in the last 180 days|domain-and-forest|privileged-access|Critical|false" "Domain controllers run a supported Windows Server version|domain-controllers|infrastructure|High|true" "The AD Recycle Bin is on|domain-and-forest|infrastructure|Medium|true" "No user has a password that never expires|directory-configuration|authentication|High|false" "Domain Admins has no more than five members|directory-configuration|privileged-access|Critical|true" "LDAP signing is required on every domain controller|domain-controllers|authentication|High|investigate" "Unconstrained delegation is not allowed on computers|directory-configuration|privileged-access|Critical|false" "SYSVOL replicates with DFSR|domain-controllers|infrastructure|Low|true"; do
  j=$((j+1)); IFS='|' read -r title feat area sev r <<< "$spec"; id="CAD.$((100+j))"
  case $r in
    true) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Checked against corp.contoso.com. (Demo data.)'
    return \$true";;
    false) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result 'Checked against corp.contoso.com: this does not meet the requirement. (Demo data.)'
    return \$false";;
    investigate) body="    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Investigate -Result 'DC02 did not answer the query. (Demo data.)'
    return \$false";;
  esac
  cat > ad/Test.$id.ps1 <<EOF
function Test-Cad$((100+j)) {
    [MaesterTest(Id = '$id', Title = '$title', Product = 'ad', Feature = '$feat', Area = '$area', ResourceType = 'DomainController', Severity = '$sev')]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()
$body
}
EOF
  printf '%s. (Demo data.)\n\n<!--- Results --->\n%%TestResult%%\n' "$title" > ad/Test.$id.md
done

Get-MtTest -Path ./scratch/bare,./scratch/ad | ? Problems | ft Id, Problems
foreach ($s in "bare","ad") { $r = Invoke-Maester -Path ./scratch/$s -SkipBuiltIn -SkipGraphConnect -NonInteractive -SkipVersionCheck -DisableTelemetry -OutputFolder ./scratch/results-$s -PassThru 6>$null; "$s : " + (($r.Tests | % { "$($_.Id)=$($_.Result)" }) -join " ") }' 2>&1 | tail -8

The review reports are ready. Open [scratch/report-variants/index.html](scratch/report-variants/index.html): it links 20 reports, covering 7 scenarios each in wordings A, B and C (the tenant scenario has only A and B). They're also open in the browser pane at http://localhost:8766/index.html.

**Wording suggestions for a run with no tenant**

| | Top bar | Eyebrow | Title |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A, neutral** (my pick) | date only | Maester report | 54% of the checks that ran passed |
| **B, machine** | Merills-MacBook-Pro | Test report, or Security report if any built-in tests ran | This run passed 54% of the checks that ran |
| **C, suite** | PoraLocal | Maester report | PoraLocal passed 54% of the checks that ran |

I recommend A. It never claims what the report is about, and "Maester report" is true whatever tests ran. B can put a machine name into a report someone shares. C depends on the suite ID, which is often something like `Custom`.

**What applies in every wording**

- **Report subject:**
  - The placeholder "TenantName (not connected to Graph)" is gone.
  - A run names its tenant if it connected to one.
  - A run connected only to Active Directory names its domain. In the AD scenario that's "corp.contoso.com passed 57%…".
- **Lead sentence:** it only says "because a service, licence or permission was missing" when that is actually why tests didn't run.
- **Runs with no scored checks:** the title says "No check gave a pass or fail" instead of "passed 0%".
- **Tests with no attributes:** the bare scenario now looks tidy.
  - No fake "Custom" product.
  - The "Critical and high" and "Quick wins" cards are hidden.
  - The "Failed by severity" card is hidden. It used to say "Nothing failed" while 3 tests had failed.
  - The fix list says the tests are listed in run order, because they declare no severity.
- **Failed by severity:** the card hides when nothing failed. A failure with no severity shows as "Not rated".
- **Wording:**
  - "Does not apply" no longer mentions "the tenant".
  - The footer says the report holds data from the subject, or "the systems its tests read".

**Things to know**

- The A/B/C switch (`window.__mtTitleVariant` in `report/src/lib/runSubject.ts`) is temporary. I'll remove the wordings you don't pick.
- PowerShell still writes the placeholder strings into the JSON; the report just ignores them now. Writing `null` there instead would be a small follow-up, but it changes the JSON other tools read.
- Two background servers are running for the browser pane, on ports 8765 and 8766.
- The `graph-connected` scenario uses the run you made against Pora.
- I checked the bare, AD, demo, Graph-offline and tenant scenarios in the pane, with no console errors. Nothing is committed.

# Environment update

While the unit tests finish (I'll commit and push once they pass), here are options for mentioning Maester Cloud. I looked for places where the report already shows a limit of a one-off local run, so the mention reads as help rather than an ad. They're ordered from most to least subtle.

**1. Where a single run falls short (my top pick)**
- **Trend card:** with only one run, the pass-rate trend is empty. Add one muted line there: *"See this trend over time: Maester Cloud runs these checks daily and keeps the history."*
- **Changes strip:** on a first run there's no "new failures since…" comparison. Show *"Get told when a result changes"* there.

These only show when the reader has hit that limit, and they disappear once there's history, so a regular user rarely sees them.

**2. Footer credit**
- Today it reads: "Generated by Maester 3.0.0 · maester.dev".
- Extend it to: "… · maester.dev · Run it on a schedule with **maester.cloud**".
- It's on every page, small and below the content. It's the most "standard" place, but it's also the most ignorable.

**3. Run details page**
- That page already explains how the report was made: the command, the machine, the duration.
- Add one row: *"Ran on Merills-MacBook-Pro. Maester Cloud can run it for you, with no machine to keep on."*
- It's a factual comparison in the place people go to learn how runs work.

**4. Action plan**
- People open the action plan to work through fixes.
- Add a note at the bottom: *"Assign these to people and track them to done in Maester Cloud."*
- This aims at the strongest buying moment, a team acting on the findings. It's a step more "salesy".

**5. Tenant switcher, for reports that combine several tenants**
- Add a line under the tenant list: *"Compare every tenant you manage, every day, in Maester Cloud."*
- It only appears in multi-tenant reports, which is your MSP and partner audience.

**6. Export menu**
- Add a last item: "Share with your team" → Maester Cloud. It sits next to the CSV and Markdown exports.
- Make it a link with a "↗", not something that pretends to share the report.

**Guardrails I'd keep for any of them**
- **One mention per page at most:** every option shows only in context, so none of them stack.
- **Plain links only:** no tracking pixel or remote image, so the report stays offline and private. A `?ref=report` on the link is enough for you to count visits.
- **A way to turn them off:** a config switch such as `Report.HideMaesterCloud`, for consultants who hand reports to their clients.
- **Never above the fold:** keep them out of the overview's header and KPI cards.

cd /Users/merill/github/maester/.claude/worktrees/zero-trust-view; gh pr create --base main --head feat/zero-trust-workshop-view --title "feat(report): Zero Trust plan view, pack menus and a neater report for local runs" --body-file - <<'EOF'
## What this changes

**Zero Trust plan (Zero Trust Assessment pack)**
- The pack bundles Microsoft's Zero Trust Workshop data and attaches it to the run as `zero-trust-workshop` (JSON).
- The report shows it as a swimlane board and a table, by pillar, functional area and lane. Each task opens in a panel with its checks and the workshop's guidance.

**Report menu**
- Azure-style hubs (products, frameworks, one per pack) beside an icon rail.
- Menus nest to any depth. They can be collapsed to the rail, opened from the rail as a flyover, and resized; the choice is remembered. On a phone the menu is a drawer.
- Old `#/zero-trust/...` links redirect.

**Pack contract**
- `Report.Navigation` in `maester-pack.json`: the pack's own menu, using the report's built-in views (pack, tests, plan, attachment, guide, about).
- `Report.Logo`: a mark the report draws in the pack's page header (`microsoft`, or a product key). The report never loads an image from a pack.
- `Read-MtPackManifest` validates both; the schema and `writing-a-pack.md` document them.

**Report polish**
- The test sheet and task panel close when you click outside them, and blur the page behind.
- Runs without a tenant: the report no longer shows "TenantName (not connected to Graph)". It names the tenant, or the AD domain for an AD-only run, or nothing, under a "Maester report" eyebrow.
- Tests that declare no severity, effort or impact no longer get empty severity and quick-win cards, or a fake "Custom" product.
- The "did not run" sentence only blames a missing service, licence or permission when that is the cause.
- Pack links point to https://packs.maester.cloud/.

## Testing
- `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1`: 7048 tests, no failures.
- `npm run build` in `report/`.
- Checked in the browser against a real Zero Trust Assessment run on a test tenant, and against generated scenarios: bare custom tests, AD-style tests with and without a domain connection, Graph tests run offline and connected.

`powershell/assets/ReportTemplate.html` is left to CI.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

intro | This is Maester: the open-source way to test your Microsoft 365 security, every day, in one run.
install | Install it from the PowerShell Gallery. Every check ships inside the module, so there's nothing else to set up.
connect | Connect Maester to your tenant. It reads your configuration with read-only permissions, and nothing leaves your tenant.
invoke | Now run Invoke-Maester. Add the Zero Trust Assessment pack, and Microsoft's own assessment runs in the same pass.
console | The console shows every product as it's tested, the checks running right now, and the results as they land: over twelve hundred checks across CIS, CISA, Microsoft's guidance and Zero Trust.
report | When the run finishes, your report opens. It tells you what to fix first, ranked by severity and effort.
detail | Every finding explains what an attacker could do, what Maester found, and exactly how to fix it.
frameworks | See where you stand against the frameworks your auditors ask about, and the attack techniques each gap leaves open.
zta | And Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment sits right alongside, in the same report.
automate | Run it every day in GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps, and know the moment something changes.
cloud | Or run it with Maester Cloud, securely, in your own Azure subscription: your data never leaves your tenant. Find out more at maester.cloud, and get started at maester.dev.

I pushed the fixes for the failed CodeQL check and the review comments to [maester365/maester#2713](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2713), in commit `53552d508`. CI hasn't re-run on it yet.

- **CodeQL, incomplete sanitization (`zeroTrust.ts`):** the workshop text now has its iframe tags removed repeatedly until none is left, so an iframe tag hidden inside another one can't survive. It wasn't exploitable before, because the report's Markdown renderer already cleans the HTML with DOMPurify. I ran a quick check with a nested-tag input and no iframe tag was left.
- **Write-Host warnings, 6 threads (`Update-MtZtWorkshopData.ps1`):** I added the same `PSAvoidUsingWriteHost` suppression, with a justification, that the other console build scripts use. PSScriptAnalyzer now reports nothing on the file.
- **Threads:** I replied to all seven threads with what changed and resolved them.

The other three comments needed no change. Codacy reported no issues, and CodeRabbit's review was still in progress. The third was the explainer reminder: the "How Maester works" explainer's narration still matches the report, but its screenshots show the old left menu. Updating them means re-recording that explainer, so I left it for now.

The full unit suite didn't run on this commit: the change is two small edits, and the TypeScript build and the analyzer both passed.

=== 4501901522
** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win**
**Validate the guide shape in `readGuide`. A malformed guide can crash the guide pages.**
`readGuide` returns any JSON object as `PackGuide`. The TypeScript types give no runtime guarantee. `Read-MtPackManifest` checks only that the guide file is a JSON object. A pack guide with `"Connect": { "Steps": "text" }`, `"Run": { "Options": "x" }` or a `null` entry in `Links` passes validation. `GuideView` in `PackRoute.tsx` then calls `.map` or `.filter` on a non-array, or reads `l.Url` on `null`. Each case throws a `TypeError` during render. The router has no error boundary, so an uncaught render error can blank the whole report.
Normalize the guide in `readGuide`. Keep only arrays of objects for `Prerequisites`, `Connect.Steps`, `Run.Commands`, `Run.Options` and `Links`. Keep only arrays of strings for `Notes`. Drop everything else.
Sketch of the fix
```diff
--- "a/report/src/lib/packNav.ts"
+++ "b/report/src/lib/packNav.ts"
@@ -59,10 +59,23 @@
   return entries.length ? entries : null
 }
+const objects = (v: unknown): Record[] | undefined =>
+  Array.isArray(v) ? v.filter((x): x is Record => !!x && typeof x === "object" && !Array.isArray(x)) : undefined
+const strings = (v: unknown): string[] | undefined => (Array.isArray(v) ? v.filter((x): x is string => typeof x === "string") : undefined)
+
 export function readGuide(value: unknown): PackGuide | null {
-  const g = parse(value)
-  return g && typeof g === "object" && !Array.isArray(g) ? g : null
+  const g = parse>(value)
+  if (!g || typeof g !== "object" || Array.isArray(g)) return null
+  const connect = g.Connect && typeof g.Connect === "object" ? (g.Connect as Record) : {}
+  const run = g.Run && typeof g.Run === "object" ? (g.Run as Record) : {}
+  return {
+    ...(g as PackGuide),
+    Prerequisites: objects(g.Prerequisites) as GuideStep[] | undefined,
+    Links: objects(g.Links) as PackGuide["Links"],
+    Connect: g.Connect ? { ...(connect as object), Steps: objects(connect.Steps) as GuideStep[] | undefined, Notes: strings(connect.Notes) } : undefined,
+    Run: g.Run ? { ...(run as object), Commands: objects(run.Commands) as GuideStep[] | undefined, Notes: strings(run.Notes), Options: objects(run.Options) as never } : undefined,
+  }
 }

```

    Run: g.Run ? { ...(run as object), Commands: objects(run.Commands) as GuideStep[] | undefined, Notes: strings(run.Notes), Options: objects(run.Options) as never } : undefined,

CodeQL reports "Incomplete multi-character sanitization" for Line 191. +# Zero Trust Workshop data for the Zero Trust plan
+The Zero Trust Assessment pack ([`packs/zero-trust-assessment`](../../packs/zero-trust-assessment)) adds the
+Microsoft Zero Trust Workshop plan to the Maester report, where the **Zero Trust plan** view shows each workshop
+task with the status of the checks that measure it. The data is in the pack's `workshop` folder.
+| File | What it holds | Kept by |

+| `identity.json`, `devices.json`, `data.json`, `network.json`, `infrastructure.json`, `security-operations.json`, `ai.json` | One pillar each: its functional areas and tasks (swimlane, phase, priority, effort, user impact, licence, CISA maturity stage, dependencies), each task's guidance and the assessment tests Microsoft maps to it (`Checks`, as `ZTA.<id>`) | `Update-MtZtWorkshopData.ps1` |
+| `icons.json` | The SVG icons the tasks and areas use | `Update-MtZtWorkshopData.ps1` |
+| `maester.json` | Maester's additions: Maester tests that measure a workshop task, a note per task, and tasks the workshop does not have | Hand |
+- Pillars, areas and tasks: `https://zerotrust.microsoft.com/data/<pillar>-pillar-data.json`. Tasks the workshop
+  task's link names. Front matter, embedded videos, the title and the effort and impact lines are removed.
+- Check mapping: `src/powershell/assets/ztw-task-mapping.json` in the same repository (MIT licence), assessment
+  test ID to workshop task IDs.
+Zero Trust Workshop content © Microsoft; guidance and check mapping from microsoft/zerotrustassessment, MIT licence.
+It takes a few minutes (one request per guidance document). Set `GITHUB_TOKEN` if the GitHub API limits you. The
+output is stable: a pillar keeps its `Updated` date unless something else in it changed, so a rerun on unchanged
+sources leaves no diff. The script warns about a mapped task no pillar shows and an icon the site does not have.
+## Add Maester tests to a task
+Edit `maester.json`. Under `Tasks`, key by the workshop task ID and list the built-in tests that measure it:
+  "RMI_001": { "Tests": ["MT.1003", "MT.1004"], "Note": "Maester also checks that the policy set has no gaps." }
+These are added after Microsoft's mapping, never instead of it. A built-in test that `taxonomy.json` lists in
+`AlsoCheckedBy` for one of the task's assessment tests is added on its own, as the same check, so it does not
+need to be listed here. `Note` is optional and shown on the task.
+A task the workshop does not have goes under `ExtraTasks`, with its `Pillar` (one of the pillar IDs above), an
+`Id` that starts with `MAE_`, the `AreaId` of an area of that pillar (as the pillar file spells it), the same
+fields as a workshop task, its `Tests`, and its guidance as Markdown in `Doc`.
+The unit tests fail when `maester.json` names a test, task, area or dependency that does not exist.

# AGENTS.md

Maester is a PowerShell framework for monitoring Microsoft 365 security
configuration, with its own test engine. Pester is used only for the module's unit tests
and to run users' Pester-format custom tests. Requires PowerShell 7.4+. Monorepo: `powershell/` (module source),
`tests/` (security checks shipped to users), `src/Maester.Engine/` (C# engine core,
built DLL committed in `powershell/lib/`), `build/`, `website/` (Astro + Starlight,
maester.dev), `report/` (React app that builds the HTML report template).

## Two unrelated test trees — don't mix them

- `tests/` — Maester **security checks** that ship to end-user tenants, run via
  `Invoke-Maester`. Each check is a native test: `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]Test.<ID>.ps1`
  (one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute) plus `Test.<ID>.md`. No
  `*.Tests.ps1` wrappers, no connection/licence guards, no outer try/catch: declare
  `Service`/`License` and the engine handles them. Scaffold with `New-MtTest`,
  validate with `Get-MtTest <ID>` (`Get-MtTest -Path` applies the rules of a custom test
  and does not report a missing attribute), run with `Invoke-MtTest -Path`; `Convert-MtTest`
  converts users' Pester-format tests. New MT.xxxx checks go here; follow
  `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` and `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`,
  and choose the attribute values with `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md`
  (see "Reviewing a test's attributes" below). A benchmark test for a requirement that another
  suite already checks is a shim that returns that test's result (see "Reviewing a test for
  duplicates" below).
- `powershell/tests/` — **unit tests for the module itself**.

## Commands

- Unit tests: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` — run before pushing. These enforce
  naming, exports, help, and PSScriptAnalyzer conventions; fix what they flag.
- Build module: `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`; validate: `./build/Test-MaesterModuleOutput.ps1`
- Website: `cd website && npm ci && npm start` · Report: `cd report && npm ci && npm run build`

## Hard rules

- Generated content — regenerate, never hand-edit: `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/versioned_docs/` (the frozen 2.x docs), everything under
  `powershell/internal/generated/`, and the native `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` and
  `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` files the generators in `build/eidsca/` and `build/orca/`
  write. Edit the PowerShell source, comment-based help or generator templates and let
  automation regenerate. `powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json` (the dashboard's
  Featured contributor list) is written by `./build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1` from
  the website's contributor data.
- Never commit the website data that each build generates: the command pages in `website/docs/commands/`
  (everything but `readme.mdx`), `website/src/data/test-catalog.json`, `contributors.json` and `sponsors.json`.
  They are ignored by git. `website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs` writes them from the module source, the git
  history and GitHub before `npm run dev` and `npm run build`; `npm run refresh-data` writes them again.
  The build-website workflow builds and deploys maester.dev from main, so a merge needs no follow-up PR.
- A test is mapped to a framework in one place: the `Control` attribute, `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. A
  CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA test `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and any other
  test may name the same requirements. An ASD test carries `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'` (or `ism:<id>` for a
  control outside the maturity model). Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its
  suite's framework. The engine builds `Benchmark` from the first `Control` that a framework file knows and adds
  that requirement's `Related` references to `Control`; do not repeat those, and do not add benchmark tags.
- A framework file is a catalogue, not a list of tests: `tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`
  (`tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json`, `tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json`,
  `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, and the generated `tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json` and
  `tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json`, written by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1` from the ISM OSCAL release),
  declared in the suite's `suite.json` (`Frameworks`: `Key`,
  `Version`). It holds the framework's name and version and each requirement's `Id` and facts (CIS `Level` and
  `Profile`; CISA `Criticality`, `Upstream` and `Related` NIST references; Essential Eight `Level` and `Strategy`;
  ISM `Guideline`, `Section` and `Applicability`), never the text of a benchmark and
  never a `Tests` list. When a new test implements a requirement the file does not have, add the requirement in
  the same commit, or `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` and the unit tests fail.
- Checks read through the session cache. A run reports on one snapshot of the tenant, so no check, pack or helper
  passes `-DisableCache` or otherwise bypasses the Graph or GitHub cache, even to read data that changed during the
  session. Only the transport helpers listed in `powershell/tests/general/GraphCacheUsage.Tests.ps1` may offer the
  switch, and that test fails on any other use. Don't apply a review suggestion to bypass the cache.

## Repository layout — where files go

Full rules and reasoning: `website/docs/contributing.md` ("Repository layout"), published at
https://maester.dev/docs/contributing#repository-layout. `powershell/tests/general/RepositoryLayout.Tests.ps1`
enforces them. When writing or reviewing a change, check every added, moved or renamed file:

- Folder names under `tests/`, `powershell/` and `build/` are lowercase kebab-case
  (`global-secure-access`, not `GlobalSecureAccess`). No two paths may differ only in case.
- One name per service, the same everywhere: `ad`, `azure`, `azure-devops`, `copilot`,
  `copilot-studio`, `defender`, `entra`, `exchange`, `fabric`, `foundry`, `github`,
  `global-secure-access`, `graph`, `intune`, `purview`, `sharepoint`, `teams`, `xspm`.
  Folders name the product whose settings a check reads, never a theme: an AI check goes in
  the folder of its product (an Entra agent identity check in `entra/`) and declares
  `Area = 'ai'`. A new service must be added to the guide and the test.
- `tests/<suite>/` holds only `Test.<ID>.ps1`, `Test.<ID>.md`, `suite.json` and `README.md`, plus the suite's
  framework files, `frameworks/<key>.json` beside its `suite.json` (lowercase key; nothing else goes in a
  `frameworks/` folder).
  Suites: `maester/<service>/` (plus `drift/`; `maester/xspm/` has its own suite.json),
  `cis/`, `cisa/<service>/`, `asd/<service>/`, `ad/<area>/`, generated `eidsca/` and `orca/`, and `custom/`
  (reserved for users; never commit tests there).
- `powershell/public/` (exported) is grouped by job: `run/`, `connect/`, `report/`, `app/`,
  `packs/`, `services/<service>/`. `powershell/internal/` uses `engine/`, `session/`, `connect/`,
  `report/`, `app/`, `packs/`, `services/<service>/`, `checks/<suite>/<service>/`, `generated/`,
  `utility/`. Nothing sits directly in `public/` or `internal/`.
- `packs/<name>/` at the repository root holds the Maester Packs that ship with Maester (ID `maester.<name>`,
  a code of the pack's own such as `ZTA`, test IDs `<Code>.<n>` without the `MP.` that installed packs use). They are not under `tests/`: a pack loads into its own private
  module, and its rows carry `Source = Custom` and `Package`. See `packs/README.md`.
- Put a function by its job, not by the check that first needed it: reusable data access
  for a service goes in `internal/services/<service>/`; logic only one suite's checks use
  goes in `internal/checks/<suite>/<service>/`; a helper users call from custom tests goes
  in `public/services/<service>/` (and in the manifest's `FunctionsToExport`).
- One function per file, named `Verb-Noun.ps1` after the function, with an approved verb.
- Custom tests can call only exported commands. To make an internal helper available to them,
  `git mv` it from `internal/services/<service>/` to `public/services/<service>/`, add it to
  `FunctionsToExport`, and give it full comment-based help (see "Making an internal helper public"
  in the contributing guide). Exporting a command makes it public API; flag a promotion in review.

## Reviewing a test for duplicates

Benchmarks overlap, and a check that CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester each implement in their own way gives
two answers for one setting and drifts with every benchmark update. When you write, change or review a
test, look for a duplicate before the attribute review:

1. Find the tests in every suite that read the same setting (`Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key>`,
   and a search of `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name).
2. If one exists, read what the benchmark asks in its own sources, not only the requirement's one-line
   text: its audit or assessment guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (for ASD, the
   ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud). Note
   every concrete value they name, and whether it differs from the existing test.
3. Decide, as "Tests that another suite already has" in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` says:
   - the benchmark asks for what the existing test checks: the new test is a shim, a test whose body is
     `return <the existing test's function>`, with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control` and guide;
   - it asks for the same check with a different value the existing test takes as a parameter: a shim
     that passes the value;
   - it asks for something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a test of its own, which
     reads data through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers instead of copying another
     test's logic.
4. Fail the review when a benchmark test re-implements a check another suite already has and the
   benchmark's sources give no reason, or when a helper named after a suite (`Get-MtAsd*`,
   `Get-MtCis*`) does data access that is not specific to that suite. Say which test it duplicates
   and which source you read.

`powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` checks the mechanical part: a shim declares the same
attribute values as the test it calls (`Product` to `Mitre`, `Service`, `License` and the other gates),
calls a test that exists and is not a shim, passes only parameters that test declares, leaves its own
requirement off that test's `Control`, and names that test in its guide. Whether the benchmark asks for
the same thing is the reviewer's judgement.

## Reviewing a test's attributes

Every built-in test declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses: `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` and, where one applies, `RelatedProduct`. The rules for each value
are in `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (the rubric); the allowed keys are in
`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`.

When you write, change or review a test, check its attributes against the rubric as a separate
step, after the code review and before you approve or hand off:

1. Read the test's `.ps1` and `.md` and state in one sentence what it checks and what the fix is.
2. For each attribute that is new or changed, decide whether the declared value fits the rubric. A
   value fails only when the rubric clearly gives a different one; say which value and which rule.
3. Fail the review if any value does not fit. Do not approve with a note to fix it later.

Three things enforce this, in order:

- `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` fails on anything mechanical: a missing
  attribute, a key that is not in the taxonomy, a retired ATT&CK technique, a taxonomy tag on a
  built-in test.
- The `attribute-review` workflow (`.github/workflows/attribute-review.yaml`) runs a reviewer model
  against the rubric on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes, and
  fails the check with the value it expected and the reason. It calls the Claude API with the
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret; without the secret it reports that the review was skipped. To run
  the same review locally before pushing, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and run
  `./build/review/Invoke-MtAttributeReview.ps1 -BaseRef origin/main -OutputPath ./TestResults`
  (`TestResults/` is ignored by git; without `-OutputPath` the report is written to the current
  folder).
- The person or agent reviewing the pull request applies the same rubric and is the last word. A
  maintainer who disagrees with the workflow can apply the `attribute-review-override` label and
  should say why in the pull request.

## Labelling pull requests, issues and discussions

Labels follow one rubric so the queue can be filtered by status, type and product. The
labels are defined in `.github/labels.json`; the rules for choosing them are in
`.github/skills/maester-triage/SKILL.md`. To triage, use the `maester-triage` agent (or follow
the skill directly): it shows its plan before changing anything and only ever changes labels.
After editing `.github/labels.json`, run `./build/github/Sync-GitHubLabels.ps1` to see the
changes and `-Apply` to make them. `-Apply` creates, renames and updates labels and copies a merged
label onto the items that carry the old one; add `-DeleteMerged` to also delete the old labels.

## Agents and skills

The agents and skills in this repository are listed in `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md`. Each
has one source file: `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` or `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The
Claude Code copies under `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`, and that docs page, are generated
from them by `./build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1`. Edit the source file, run the script, and
commit both; never edit a generated copy. `powershell/tests/general/AgentFiles.Tests.ps1` fails
when they drift.

- [Contributors attribution system](contributors-attribution-system.md) — registry + git-derived credits for maester.dev
- [Maester 3.0 design](maester-3-design.md) — design doc, owner rulings, status (M0–M9 done on PR 2334, design changes awaiting sign-off)
- [Maester Packs design](maester-marketplace-design.md) — packs/connectors marketplace draft + mockup; owner rulings 2026-10-07, some items open
- [Maester 3.0 console output](maester-3-console-output.md) — TUI/perf rulings 2026-10-10, shipped on PR 2334, open follow-ups; 2026-10-18 boxed main column + pipeline built (uncommitted branch)
- [Test taxonomy research](maester-test-taxonomy-research.md) — framework/MITRE mapping research + clean-slate attribute design; lives in maester-cloud, never in Maester; Category/Tag may change

# AGENTS.md

Maester is a PowerShell framework for monitoring Microsoft 365 security
configuration, with its own test engine. Pester is used only for the module's unit tests
and to run users' Pester-format custom tests. Requires PowerShell 7.4+. Monorepo: `powershell/` (module source),
`tests/` (security checks shipped to users), `src/Maester.Engine/` (C# engine core,
built DLL committed in `powershell/lib/`), `build/`, `website/` (Astro + Starlight,
maester.dev), `report/` (React app that builds the HTML report template).

## Two unrelated test trees — don't mix them

- `tests/` — Maester **security checks** that ship to end-user tenants, run via
  `Invoke-Maester`. Each check is a native test: `tests/<suite>/[<service>/]Test.<ID>.ps1`
  (one function with a `[MaesterTest(...)]` attribute) plus `Test.<ID>.md`. No
  `*.Tests.ps1` wrappers, no connection/licence guards, no outer try/catch: declare
  `Service`/`License` and the engine handles them. Scaffold with `New-MtTest`,
  validate with `Get-MtTest <ID>` (`Get-MtTest -Path` applies the rules of a custom test
  and does not report a missing attribute), run with `Invoke-MtTest -Path`; `Convert-MtTest`
  converts users' Pester-format tests. New MT.xxxx checks go here; follow
  `.github/skills/maester-test-expert/SKILL.md` and `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx`,
  and choose the attribute values with `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md`
  (see "Reviewing a test's attributes" below). A benchmark test for a requirement that another
  suite already checks is a shim that returns that test's result (see "Reviewing a test for
  duplicates" below).
- `powershell/tests/` — **unit tests for the module itself**.

## Commands

- Unit tests: `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` — run before pushing. These enforce
  naming, exports, help, and PSScriptAnalyzer conventions; fix what they flag.
- Build module: `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1`; validate: `./build/Test-MaesterModuleOutput.ps1`
- Website: `cd website && npm ci && npm start` · Report: `cd report && npm ci && npm run build`

## Hard rules

- Generated content — regenerate, never hand-edit: `website/src/data/versions.json`, `website/versioned_docs/` (the frozen 2.x docs), everything under
  `powershell/internal/generated/`, and the native `tests/eidsca/Test.EIDSCA.*` and
  `tests/orca/Test.ORCA.*` files the generators in `build/eidsca/` and `build/orca/`
  write. Edit the PowerShell source, comment-based help or generator templates and let
  automation regenerate. `powershell/assets/ConsoleContributors.json` (the dashboard's
  Featured contributor list) is written by `./build/Update-ConsoleContributors.ps1` from
  the website's contributor data.
- Never commit the website data that each build generates: the command pages in `website/docs/commands/`
  (everything but `readme.mdx`), `website/src/data/test-catalog.json`, `contributors.json` and `sponsors.json`.
  They are ignored by git. `website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs` writes them from the module source, the git
  history and GitHub before `npm run dev` and `npm run build`; `npm run refresh-data` writes them again.
  The build-website workflow builds and deploys maester.dev from main, so a merge needs no follow-up PR.
- A test is mapped to a framework in one place: the `Control` attribute, `<framework-key>:<requirement-id>`. A
  CIS test carries `Control = 'cis-m365:5.1.5.1'`, a CISA test `Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.1'`, and any other
  test may name the same requirements. An ASD test carries `Control = 'essential-eight:ISM-1504'` (or `ism:<id>` for a
  control outside the maturity model). Every test in `tests/cis`, `tests/cisa` and `tests/asd` must name a requirement of its
  suite's framework. The engine builds `Benchmark` from the first `Control` that a framework file knows and adds
  that requirement's `Related` references to `Control`; do not repeat those, and do not add benchmark tags.
- A framework file is a catalogue, not a list of tests: `tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json`
  (`tests/cis/frameworks/cis-m365.json`, `tests/cis/frameworks/cis-github.json`,
  `tests/cisa/frameworks/cisa-scuba.json`, and the generated `tests/asd/frameworks/essential-eight.json` and
  `tests/asd/frameworks/ism.json`, written by `build/asd/Update-AsdFramework.ps1` from the ISM OSCAL release),
  declared in the suite's `suite.json` (`Frameworks`: `Key`,
  `Version`). It holds the framework's name and version and each requirement's `Id` and facts (CIS `Level` and
  `Profile`; CISA `Criticality`, `Upstream` and `Related` NIST references; Essential Eight `Level` and `Strategy`;
  ISM `Guideline`, `Section` and `Applicability`), never the text of a benchmark and
  never a `Tests` list. When a new test implements a requirement the file does not have, add the requirement in
  the same commit, or `./build/Build-MaesterModule.ps1` and the unit tests fail.
- Checks read through the session cache. A run reports on one snapshot of the tenant, so no check, pack or helper
  passes `-DisableCache` or otherwise bypasses the Graph or GitHub cache, even to read data that changed during the
  session. Only the transport helpers listed in `powershell/tests/general/GraphCacheUsage.Tests.ps1` may offer the
  switch, and that test fails on any other use. Don't apply a review suggestion to bypass the cache.

## Repository layout — where files go

Full rules and reasoning: `website/docs/contributing.md` ("Repository layout"), published at
https://maester.dev/docs/contributing#repository-layout. `powershell/tests/general/RepositoryLayout.Tests.ps1`
enforces them. When writing or reviewing a change, check every added, moved or renamed file:

- Folder names under `tests/`, `powershell/` and `build/` are lowercase kebab-case
  (`global-secure-access`, not `GlobalSecureAccess`). No two paths may differ only in case.
- One name per service, the same everywhere: `ad`, `azure`, `azure-devops`, `copilot`,
  `copilot-studio`, `defender`, `entra`, `exchange`, `fabric`, `foundry`, `github`,
  `global-secure-access`, `graph`, `intune`, `purview`, `sharepoint`, `teams`, `xspm`.
  Folders name the product whose settings a check reads, never a theme: an AI check goes in
  the folder of its product (an Entra agent identity check in `entra/`) and declares
  `Area = 'ai'`. A new service must be added to the guide and the test.
- `tests/<suite>/` holds only `Test.<ID>.ps1`, `Test.<ID>.md`, `suite.json` and `README.md`, plus the suite's
  framework files, `frameworks/<key>.json` beside its `suite.json` (lowercase key; nothing else goes in a
  `frameworks/` folder).
  Suites: `maester/<service>/` (plus `drift/`; `maester/xspm/` has its own suite.json),
  `cis/`, `cisa/<service>/`, `asd/<service>/`, `ad/<area>/`, generated `eidsca/` and `orca/`, and `custom/`
  (reserved for users; never commit tests there).
- `powershell/public/` (exported) is grouped by job: `run/`, `connect/`, `report/`, `app/`,
  `packs/`, `services/<service>/`. `powershell/internal/` uses `engine/`, `session/`, `connect/`,
  `report/`, `app/`, `packs/`, `services/<service>/`, `checks/<suite>/<service>/`, `generated/`,
  `utility/`. Nothing sits directly in `public/` or `internal/`.
- `packs/<name>/` at the repository root holds the Maester Packs that ship with Maester (ID `maester.<name>`,
  a code of the pack's own such as `ZTA`, test IDs `<Code>.<n>` without the `MP.` that installed packs use). They are not under `tests/`: a pack loads into its own private
  module, and its rows carry `Source = Custom` and `Package`. See `packs/README.md`.
- Put a function by its job, not by the check that first needed it: reusable data access
  for a service goes in `internal/services/<service>/`; logic only one suite's checks use
  goes in `internal/checks/<suite>/<service>/`; a helper users call from custom tests goes
  in `public/services/<service>/` (and in the manifest's `FunctionsToExport`).
- One function per file, named `Verb-Noun.ps1` after the function, with an approved verb.
- Custom tests can call only exported commands. To make an internal helper available to them,
  `git mv` it from `internal/services/<service>/` to `public/services/<service>/`, add it to
  `FunctionsToExport`, and give it full comment-based help (see "Making an internal helper public"
  in the contributing guide). Exporting a command makes it public API; flag a promotion in review.

## Reviewing a test for duplicates

Benchmarks overlap, and a check that CIS, CISA, ASD and Maester each implement in their own way gives
two answers for one setting and drifts with every benchmark update. When you write, change or review a
test, look for a duplicate before the attribute review:

1. Find the tests in every suite that read the same setting (`Get-MtTest -Product <key> -Feature <key>`,
   and a search of `tests/` for the Graph endpoint or setting name).
2. If one exists, read what the benchmark asks in its own sources, not only the requirement's one-line
   text: its audit or assessment guidance and any reference configuration it publishes (for ASD, the
   ISM, the Essential Eight assessment process guide and the ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud). Note
   every concrete value they name, and whether it differs from the existing test.
3. Decide, as "Tests that another suite already has" in `website/docs/writing-tests/index.mdx` says:
   - the benchmark asks for what the existing test checks: the new test is a shim, a test whose body is
     `return <the existing test's function>`, with its own `Id`, `Title`, `Control` and guide;
   - it asks for the same check with a different value the existing test takes as a parameter: a shim
     that passes the value;
   - it asks for something no test checks, or a rule no parameter covers: a test of its own, which
     reads data through `powershell/internal/services/<service>/` helpers instead of copying another
     test's logic.
4. Fail the review when a benchmark test re-implements a check another suite already has and the
   benchmark's sources give no reason, or when a helper named after a suite (`Get-MtAsd*`,
   `Get-MtCis*`) does data access that is not specific to that suite. Say which test it duplicates
   and which source you read.

`powershell/tests/general/TestShims.Tests.ps1` checks the mechanical part: a shim declares the same
attribute values as the test it calls (`Product` to `Mitre`, `Service`, `License` and the other gates),
calls a test that exists and is not a shim, passes only parameters that test declares, leaves its own
requirement off that test's `Control`, and names that test in its guide. Whether the benchmark asks for
the same thing is the reviewer's judgement.

## Reviewing a test's attributes

Every built-in test declares what it is about, how urgent a failure is and which attack techniques
it addresses: `Product`, `Feature`, `Area`, `ResourceType`, `Severity`, `UserImpact`,
`ImplementationCost`, `Mitre` and, where one applies, `RelatedProduct`. The rules for each value
are in `website/docs/writing-tests/attribute-rubric.md` (the rubric); the allowed keys are in
`powershell/assets/MaesterTaxonomy.psd1`.

When you write, change or review a test, check its attributes against the rubric as a separate
step, after the code review and before you approve or hand off:

1. Read the test's `.ps1` and `.md` and state in one sentence what it checks and what the fix is.
2. For each attribute that is new or changed, decide whether the declared value fits the rubric. A
   value fails only when the rubric clearly gives a different one; say which value and which rule.
3. Fail the review if any value does not fit. Do not approve with a note to fix it later.

Three things enforce this, in order:

- `powershell/tests/general/NativeTestAttributes.Tests.ps1` fails on anything mechanical: a missing
  attribute, a key that is not in the taxonomy, a retired ATT&CK technique, a taxonomy tag on a
  built-in test.
- The `attribute-review` workflow (`.github/workflows/attribute-review.yaml`) runs a reviewer model
  against the rubric on every pull request that adds a test or changes one of these attributes, and
  fails the check with the value it expected and the reason. It calls the Claude API with the
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` secret; without the secret it reports that the review was skipped. To run
  the same review locally before pushing, set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and run
  `./build/review/Invoke-MtAttributeReview.ps1 -BaseRef origin/main -OutputPath ./TestResults`
  (`TestResults/` is ignored by git; without `-OutputPath` the report is written to the current
  folder).
- The person or agent reviewing the pull request applies the same rubric and is the last word. A
  maintainer who disagrees with the workflow can apply the `attribute-review-override` label and
  should say why in the pull request.

## Labelling pull requests, issues and discussions

Labels follow one rubric so the queue can be filtered by status, type and product. The
labels are defined in `.github/labels.json`; the rules for choosing them are in
`.github/skills/maester-triage/SKILL.md`. To triage, use the `maester-triage` agent (or follow
the skill directly): it shows its plan before changing anything and only ever changes labels.
After editing `.github/labels.json`, run `./build/github/Sync-GitHubLabels.ps1` to see the
changes and `-Apply` to make them. `-Apply` creates, renames and updates labels and copies a merged
label onto the items that carry the old one; add `-DeleteMerged` to also delete the old labels.

## Agents and skills

The agents and skills in this repository are listed in `website/docs/agents-and-skills.md`. Each
has one source file: `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md` or `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. The
Claude Code copies under `.claude/agents/` and `.claude/skills/`, and that docs page, are generated
from them by `./build/github/Update-AgentFiles.ps1`. Edit the source file, run the script, and
commit both; never edit a generated copy. `powershell/tests/general/AgentFiles.Tests.ps1` fails
when they drift.
